book_name: 英语词汇的奥秘（六级版）

chapters.name: 词根 1. abol = do away with 消除

words.ex: The government decided to abolish the old law.
words.ex_cn: 政府决定废除这项旧法律。
words.en: If someone in authority abolishes a system or practice, they formally put an end to it.

words.ex: The abolishment of the law made people happier.
words.ex_cn: 这项法律的废止让人们更开心了。
words.en: The act of formally ending or stopping something, such as a system, practice, or institution.

chapters.name: 词根 2. act = do, drive 做，行动

words.tr: v. 激活；使活动；使活化；
words.ex: Press the button to activate the device.
words.ex_cn: 按下按钮来激活设备。
words.en: If a device or process is activated, it starts working or becomes operational.

words.ex: The school organized a fun activity for the students.
words.ex_cn: 学校为学生们组织了一场有趣的活动。
words.en: An activity is something that you spend time doing.

words.ex: He is an activist who helps the poor.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位帮助穷人的积极分子。
words.en: An activist is a person who works to bring about political or social change by campaigning, public speaking, or demonstrating.

words.tr: v. 制定（法律）；通过（法律）；扮演（角色）
words.ex: The government will enact a new law next month.
words.ex_cn: 政府下个月将颁布一项新法律。
words.en: To enact a law or rule means to make it official by passing it through a legislative body.

words.tr: v. 互相作用；互相影响；交流；沟通；
words.ex: The two chemicals interact when mixed.
words.ex_cn: 这两种化学物质混合时会互相作用。
words.en: If people interact with each other, they communicate or work together.

words.ex: The reactor produces electricity for the city.
words.ex_cn: 这个反应堆为城市发电。
words.en: A reactor is a device or structure in which nuclear fission or fusion reactions are initiated, controlled, and sustained.

chapters.name: 词根 3. advant = ahead 前面

words.ex: It is advantageous to wake up early.
words.ex_cn: 早起是有利的。
words.en: If something is advantageous to you, it is likely to benefit you.

chapters.name: 词根 4. aeri = air 空气

words.ex: The birds flew through the aerial sky.
words.ex_cn: 鸟儿在空中飞翔。
words.en: An aerial is a wire or rod that sends or receives radio or television signals. As an adjective, aerial describes things that are in the air or related to the air.

chapters.name: 词根 5. ag = do, act 做，动

words.ex: We will review the meeting agenda tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我们明天将审查会议议程。
words.en: An agenda is a list or plan of things to be done or considered, especially in a meeting.

words.ex: He tried to agitate the workers to strike.
words.ex_cn: 他试图鼓动工人罢工。
words.en: If you agitate something, you stir it up or shake it. If something agitates you, it makes you feel anxious or upset.

words.tr: n. 搅动；煽动；激动；不安
words.ex: The agitation of the water made the dirt rise.
words.ex_cn: 水的搅动使灰尘浮起。
words.en: Agitation is a state of anxiety or nervous excitement.

chapters.name: 词根 6. agon = struggle 挣扎

words.ex: He screamed in agony after the fall.
words.ex_cn: 他摔倒后痛苦地大叫。
words.en: Agony is very severe physical or mental pain.

chapters.name: 词根 7. alb = white 白色

words.ex: He flipped through the album with old photos.
words.ex_cn: 他翻看着装满旧照片的相册。
words.en: An album is a collection of several pieces of music, songs, or photographs that are intended to form a single item.

chapters.name: 词根 8. ali = other 其他的

words.tr:
n. 外星人；外国人；外侨；
adj. 外国的；陌生的；相异的；
words.ex: The boy saw an alien in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 男孩在森林里看到了一个外星人。
words.en: An alien is someone who is not a citizen of the country in which they live, or a creature from outer space.

words.ex: His rude behavior alienated his friends.
words.ex_cn: 他粗鲁的行为使朋友们疏远了他。
words.en: To cause someone to feel isolated or estranged; to transfer the ownership of property to another.

words.ex: The long silence caused alienation between them.
words.ex_cn: 长久的沉默导致了他们之间的离间。
words.en: Alienation refers to the state or experience of being isolated from a group or an activity to which one should belong or in which one should be involved.

chapters.name: 词根 9. altern = change 改变

words.tr:
adj. 交替的；轮流的；间隔的；
v. （使）交替；（使）轮流；
words.ex: We take alternate days off work.
words.ex_cn: 我们隔天休息一次。
words.en: If something alternates between two things, it repeatedly changes from one to the other and back again.

words.tr: n. 替代选择；替代选择（alternative 的复数）；
words.ex: We need to find better alternatives to plastic.
words.ex_cn: 我们需要找到比塑料更好的替代选择。
words.en: An alternative is something that you can choose to do or use instead of something else.

chapters.name: 词根 10. am, ami = love 爱

words.tr: adj. 和蔼可亲的；亲切友好的
words.ex: He is an amiable man who always smiles.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个和蔼可亲的人，总是面带微笑。
words.en: Someone who is amiable is friendly and pleasant to be with.

words.tr:
n. 业余爱好者；
adj. 业余的；
words.ex: He is an amateur who paints on weekends.
words.ex_cn: 他是个周末画画的业余爱好者。
words.en: An amateur is someone who does something as a hobby and not as a job.

chapters.name: 词根 11. ambi = both 两边的

words.tr: adj. 模棱两可的；含糊不清的；
words.ex: His answer was ambiguous and confused everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答模棱两可，让所有人都感到困惑。
words.en: If you describe something as ambiguous, you mean that it is unclear or confusing because it can be understood in more than one way.

chapters.name: 词根 12. ampl = big 大的

words.ex: This is a good example of teamwork.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个团队合作的好例子。
words.en: An example is a particular instance of something that is representative of a group or used to illustrate a point.

words.ex: The speaker will amplify the sound for everyone to hear.
words.ex_cn: 扬声器会放大声音，让每个人都能听到。
words.en: To amplify something means to make it louder, stronger, or more detailed.

words.ex: The amplifier gives amplification to the sound.
words.ex_cn: 放大器对声音进行放大。
words.en: The process of increasing the volume, extent, or significance of something.

words.ex: The amplitude of the sound is very high.
words.ex_cn: 声音的振幅非常高。
words.en: The extent or range of a quality, property, process, or phenomenon: magnitude.

chapters.name: 词根 13. antiq = old 古老的

words.tr:
adj. 古老的；
n. 古董；
words.ex: He bought an antique chair from the old market.
words.ex_cn: 他从旧市场买了一把古老的椅子。
words.en: Something that is antique is old and often valuable because it is rare or well made.

chapters.name: 词根 14. angul = angle 角

words.ex: The pizza was cut into a triangular shape.
words.ex_cn: 比萨被切成三角形。
words.en: Something that is triangular has three straight sides and three angles, or is shaped like a triangle.

words.tr: n. 成三角形；三角关系
words.ex: The triangularity of the plot of land made it ideal for a triangular park.
words.ex_cn: 这块土地的三角形状使其非常适合建一个三角形公园。
words.en: The quality or state of being triangular.

words.ex: The table has a rectangular shape.
words.ex_cn: 这张桌子是矩形的。
words.en: Something that is rectangular has the shape of a rectangle.

words.ex: The box has a rectangle shape.
words.ex_cn: 这个盒子是长方形的。
words.en: A rectangle is a four-sided flat shape where every interior angle is a right angle (90°). Opposite sides are parallel and of equal length.

chapters.name: 词根 15. anim = mind 心神

words.ex: The team was unanimous in choosing the new leader.
words.ex_cn: 团队在选择新领导时意见完全一致。
words.en: When a group of people are unanimous, they all agree about something or all vote for the same thing.

chapters.name: 词根 16. ann = year 年

words.ex: They celebrated their wedding anniversary with dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他们用晚餐庆祝结婚纪念日。
words.en: An anniversary is a date which is remembered or celebrated because a special event happened on that date in a previous year.

words.tr: adv. 每年地；一年一次地；
words.ex: He visits his parents annually.
words.ex_cn: 他每年去看望他的父母。
words.en: Happening once every year.

chapters.name: 词根 17. aqu = water 水

words.tr: adj. 不透明的；难懂的；晦涩的
words.ex: The glass is opaque, so I cannot see through it.
words.ex_cn: 这扇玻璃是不透明的，所以我看不到它后面的东西。
words.en: If an object or substance is opaque, you cannot see through it.

chapters.name: 词根 18. arbitr = judge 判断

words.ex: The teacher chose an arbitrary number to start the game.
words.ex_cn: 老师随意选了一个数字来开始游戏。
words.en: If you describe an action, rule, or decision as arbitrary, you think that it is not based on any principle, plan, or system. It often seems unfair because of this.

words.ex: The teacher's decision seemed like arbitrariness.
words.ex_cn: 老师的决定看起来像是随意的。
words.en: The quality of being based on random choice or personal whim, rather than any reason or system.

chapters.name: 词根 19. arc, arch = bow 弓

words.tr:
v. 成弧线；
n. 弧；弧形物；
words.ex: The rainbow arcs across the sky.
words.ex_cn: 彩虹在天空中形成一道弧线。
words.en: An arc is a smoothly curving line or movement.

words.ex: The bridge has a stone arch.
words.ex_cn: 这座桥有一个石拱。
words.en: An arch is a structure that is curved at the top and is usually made of stone or brick. Arches are often used to support the weight of a bridge or the roof of a building.

chapters.name: 词根 20. arch, archy = ruler, rule 统治者，统治

words.ex: He is an architect who designs houses.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位设计房屋的建筑师。
words.en: An architect is a person who designs buildings and advises in their construction.

words.ex: He studies architecture at university.
words.ex_cn: 他在大学学习建筑学。
words.en: Architecture is the art and science of designing buildings and other physical structures.

words.tr: n. 层次体系；等级制度；
words.ex: The company has a clear hierarchy from manager to worker.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司有一个从经理到员工的明确层次体系。
words.en: A hierarchy is a system in which people or things are arranged according to their importance.

words.ex: The monarch ruled the country for 50 years.
words.ex_cn: 这位君主统治这个国家长达50年。
words.en: A monarch is a king, queen, emperor, or empress.

words.tr: adj. 君主的，国王的；君主政治的
words.ex: The country has a monarchical system of government.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家实行君主制政府体系。
words.en: Relating to a monarch or monarchy.

chapters.name: 词根 21. arm = weapon 武器

words.ex: The knight wore heavy armor in the battle.
words.ex_cn: 骑士在战斗中穿着沉重的盔甲。
words.en: Armor is a protective covering that is used to prevent damage from being inflicted to an object, individual, or vehicle by direct contact weapons or projectiles, usually during combat.

chapters.name: 词根 22. astr(o) = star 星星

words.ex: He loves watching stars and learning astronomy.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢看星星并学习天文学。
words.en: Astronomy is the scientific study of celestial objects, space, and the physical universe as a whole.

words.ex: The cost of the project is astronomic.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目的成本极其高昂。
words.en: Astronomic refers to something that is related to astronomy or is extremely large in size or amount.

words.ex: The storm caused disastrous damage to the village.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴给村庄造成了灾难性的破坏。
words.en: If you describe something as disastrous, you mean that it is very unfortunate or unsuccessful.

chapters.name: 词根 23. auct, aug = increase 增加

words.ex: The old painting was sold at an auction.
words.ex_cn: 那幅旧画在拍卖会上被卖出了。
words.en: An auction is a public sale where goods or property are sold to the highest bidder.

words.tr: v. 开创；为（某人）举行就职典礼；为…举行开幕仪式
words.ex: The president will inaugurate the new hospital next week.
words.ex_cn: 总统将于下周为新医院举行揭幕仪式。
words.en: If you inaugurate a new system, service, or project, you start it or introduce it officially.

chapters.name: 词根 24. audit = hear 听

words.ex: The auditory system helps us hear sounds.
words.ex_cn: 听觉系统帮助我们听到声音。
words.en: Relating to the sense of hearing.

words.tr:
n. 试听；试唱；试演；听力
v. 试听；试音；试镜；让…试演
words.ex: He went to an audition for the school play.
words.ex_cn: 他去参加学校话剧的试听。
words.en: An audition is a short performance given by an actor, dancer, or musician so that someone can decide if they are good enough to be in a play, film, or orchestra.

chapters.name: 词根 25. author = power 权力

words.tr: n. 权威；官方机构；权力；权威人士；当局；
words.ex: The teacher is an authority on ancient history.
words.ex_cn: 这位老师是古代史方面的权威。
words.en: The power to make decisions or enforce rules.

words.ex: The teacher gave an authoritative answer.
words.ex_cn: 老师给出了一个权威性的回答。
words.en: If something is authoritative, it is respected and accepted as true or correct because it comes from a reliable source.

words.ex: The teacher answered the question authoritatively.
words.ex_cn: 老师权威地回答了这个问题。
words.en: In a way that shows confidence and the expectation of being obeyed.

words.ex: The manager will authorize the payment tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 经理明天将批准这笔付款。
words.en: To give official permission for something to happen, or to give someone official permission to do something.

chapters.name: 词根 26. avi = bird 鸟

words.tr: n. 航空；航空学；飞行（术）；
words.ex: He works in aviation as a pilot.
words.ex_cn: 他作为一名飞行员从事航空工作。
words.en: Aviation is the operation and production of aircraft.

words.tr: n. 飞行员；飞机驾驶员
words.ex: The aviator flew a plane over the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 飞行员驾机飞越了山脉。
words.en: An aviator is a person who flies an aircraft.

words.tr: n. 女飞行员；女驾驶员
words.ex: The aviatrix flew her plane across the ocean.
words.ex_cn: 这位女飞行员驾驶她的飞机飞越了海洋。
words.en: A female pilot; a woman who flies an aircraft.

chapters.name: 词根 27. ban = prohibit 禁止

words.ex: He abandoned his car in the snow.
words.ex_cn: 他把车抛弃在雪地里。
words.en: If you abandon a place, thing, or person, you leave the place, thing, or person permanently or for a long time, especially when you should not do so.

words.ex: The king banish the traitor from the kingdom.
words.ex_cn: 国王将叛徒驱逐出王国。
words.en: To banish someone means to send them away from a country or place and not allow them to return.

words.tr: n. 放逐；流放；驱逐出境
words.ex: He was sentenced to banishment for his crimes.
words.ex_cn: 他因犯罪被判处流放。
words.en: The act of forcing someone to leave a country or place and not allowing them to return.

chapters.name: 词根 28. band = strip 带子

words.tr:
n. 绷带
v. 用绷带包扎
words.ex: He put a bandage on his cut finger.
words.ex_cn: 他在他割伤的手指上贴了绷带。
words.en: A bandage is a piece of material used to cover a wound or to support an injured part of the body.

chapters.name: 词根 29. bark = boat 船

words.ex: He decided to embark on a new career.
words.ex_cn: 他决定从事一份新职业。
words.en: To embark on something means to start it, especially something new, difficult, or exciting.

chapters.name: 词根 30. baro = man 男人

words.ex: The baron owns a large castle in the countryside.
words.ex_cn: 男爵拥有一座位于乡村的大城堡。
words.en: A baron is a man who is a member of the lowest rank of the nobility, or a powerful businessman with great influence in a particular industry.

words.tr: n. 男爵夫人；女男爵；（欧洲某些国家）男爵之女
words.ex: The baroness owns a large castle in the countryside.
words.ex_cn: 女男爵拥有一座位于乡村的大城堡。
words.en: A baroness is a woman who holds the rank of baron in her own right or is the wife or widow of a baron.

chapters.name: 词根 31. barr = stick 棒，栏杆

words.tr:
n. 路障；栅栏；阻碍
v. 设路障；阻挡
words.ex: The police put up a barricade to stop the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 警察设了一个路障来阻止人群。
words.en: A barricade is a temporary structure that is built across a road, entrance, or other route to prevent people from passing. It can also refer to the act of creating such a structure.

words.ex: The fence is a barrier to animals.
words.ex_cn: 这道围栏是动物的障碍。
words.en: A barrier is something such as a rule, law, or policy that makes it difficult or impossible for something to happen or be achieved.

words.ex: He embarrassed himself in front of the class.
words.ex_cn: 他在全班同学面前让自己丢脸了。
words.en: If you embarrass someone, you make them feel shy, ashamed, or guilty about something.

words.tr: adj. 令人尴尬的；令人为难的； v. “embarrass”的现在分词；
words.ex: It was embarrassing when I tripped in front of everyone.
words.ex_cn: 我在大家面前绊倒了，很尴尬。
words.en: Something that is embarrassing makes you feel shy or ashamed.

words.ex: He felt embarrassment when he tripped in front of everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他在众人面前绊倒时感到窘迫。
words.en: A feeling of self-consciousness, shame, or awkwardness.

chapters.name: 词根 32. bat = beat 打

words.tr:
n. 击球员；
v. 连续猛击；
words.ex: The batter hit a home run in the ninth inning.
words.ex_cn: 击球员在第九局击出了全垒打。
words.en: To batter something means to hit it hard many times, often causing a lot of damage. In sports, a batter is the player who is trying to hit the ball in games like baseball or cricket. Batter can also refer to a mixture of flour, eggs, and milk or water, used to make pancakes or to coat food before frying.

words.tr:
adj. 破旧不堪的；受虐待的
v. 连续猛击；殴打；严重破坏；“batter”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He had a battered old bike.
words.ex_cn: 他有一辆破旧的自行车。
words.en: Damaged by being used a lot or hit repeatedly; also, subjected to physical violence.

words.tr:
v. 防止；战斗；抑制；
n. 战斗；
words.ex: The new law aims to combat pollution.
words.ex_cn: 这项新法律旨在防止污染。
words.en: Combat refers to fighting, especially during a war. It can also mean to try to stop something harmful from happening or increasing.

chapters.name: 词根 33. bed = range 范围

words.ex: He embeds the photo in the document.
words.ex_cn: 他把照片插入到文档中。
words.en: To fix something firmly and deeply in a surrounding mass.

chapters.name: 词根 34. bell = fight 打斗

words.ex: The rebellion against the king failed.
words.ex_cn: 反对国王的叛乱失败了。
words.en: A rebellion is an organized attempt to overthrow a government or authority by a group of people.

chapters.name: 词根 35. bene = good 善，好

words.ex: Eating vegetables is beneficial to your health.
words.ex_cn: 吃蔬菜对你的健康有益。
words.en: Promoting or enhancing well-being; advantageous.

chapters.name: 词根 36. bever = drink 喝

words.ex: He drinks a cold beverage after work.
words.ex_cn: 他下班后喝一杯冷饮。
words.en: A drink, especially one other than water; a liquid for drinking.

chapters.name: 词根 37. bine = tie 捆

words.ex: She combines flour and water to make dough.
words.ex_cn: 她把面粉和水混合在一起做面团。
words.en: To combine means to join or merge two or more things together to form a single entity.

words.ex: The lock uses a simple combination of three numbers.
words.ex_cn: 这个锁使用三个数字的简单组合。
words.en: A combination is a mixture of things or people that are combined.

chapters.name: 词根 38. bio = life 生命，生物

words.ex: He is learning biochemistry at university.
words.ex_cn: 他正在大学学习生物化学。
words.en: The branch of science concerned with the chemical processes occurring within living organisms.

chapters.name: 词根 39. body = body 身体，形体

words.tr: v. 体现；使具体化；包含
words.ex: He embodies kindness and patience.
words.ex_cn: 他体现了善良和耐心。
words.en: To embody means to represent a quality or an idea exactly; to include or contain something.

chapters.name: 词根 40. bon = good 好的

words.tr: n. 奖金；红利；额外津贴；
words.ex: He received a bonus for working overtime.
words.ex_cn: 他因加班获得了奖金。
words.en: A bonus is an extra amount of money that is added to someone's pay, usually because they have worked very hard.

chapters.name: 词根 41. botan = herb 草

words.ex: He loves studying botany in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢在花园里学习植物学。
words.en: Botany is the scientific study of plants.

words.ex: The botanist studies plants in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 这位植物学家在森林里研究植物。
words.en: A botanist is a scientist who studies plants.

words.ex: The garden has a botanical section for native plants.
words.ex_cn: 这个花园有一个专门种植本地植物的植物区。
words.en: Relating to plants or the scientific study of plants.

chapters.name: 词根 42. bourg = town 市镇

words.tr:
n. 中产阶级的人；资产阶级的人
adj. 中产阶级的；追求名利的；资产阶级的
words.ex: He lives a bourgeois life with a big house and a car.
words.ex_cn: 他过着资产阶级的生活，有一栋大房子和一辆车。
words.en: If you describe people, their way of life, or their attitudes as bourgeois, you are criticizing them for caring too much about money and possessions and for being too conventional.

chapters.name: 词根 43. brace = two arms 两臂

words.tr:
n. 支撑物；支架；牙箍
v. 支撑；绷紧；紧靠；准备好
words.ex: The old bookshelf needs a brace to stay steady.
words.ex_cn: 旧书架需要一个支撑物来保持稳定。
words.en: To brace oneself means to prepare oneself for something difficult or unpleasant.

words.tr: v. 拥抱；包含（embrace 的现在分词）；
words.ex: She is embracing her little brother.
words.ex_cn: 她正在拥抱她的弟弟。
words.en: To hold someone closely in one's arms, especially as a sign of affection; to accept or support a belief, theory, or change willingly and enthusiastically.

words.ex: He finally embraced the new idea.
words.ex_cn: 他最终接受了这个新想法。
words.en: To take someone into your arms as a sign of love or affection, or to accept something enthusiastically.

chapters.name: 词根 44. brev = short 短的

words.ex: He used an abbreviation for 'company' in his note.
words.ex_cn: 他在笔记中用了'company'的缩写。
words.en: An abbreviation is a shortened form of a word or phrase.

words.ex: He abbreviates the word 'example' as 'ex.'.
words.ex_cn: 他把单词 'example' 缩写为 'ex.'。
words.en: To abbreviate something means to make it shorter, especially by using a particular word or phrase to represent it.

chapters.name: 词根 45. brilli = sparkle 发光

words.tr: adj. 卓越的；极好的；明亮的；灿烂的；
words.ex: He gave a brilliant answer to the math question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这道数学题给出了卓越的回答。
words.en: A brilliant person, idea, or performance is extremely clever or skilful.

chapters.name: 词根 46. broid = twist 扭

words.ex: She made an embroidery of a flower on the pillow.
words.ex_cn: 她在枕头上绣了一朵花。
words.en: Embroidery is the craft of decorating fabric or other materials using a needle to apply thread or yarn. It may also incorporate other materials such as pearls, beads, quills, and sequins.

chapters.name: 词根 47. cad, cas, cay, cid = fall 落下，降临

words.ex: The accident caused many casualties.
words.ex_cn: 这场事故造成了许多伤亡人员。
words.en: A casualty is a person who is killed or injured in a war or in an accident.

words.ex: His opinion coincides with mine.
words.ex_cn: 他的观点与我的一致。
words.en: If one event coincides with another, they happen at the same time.

words.ex: It's a coincidence that we both wore blue today.
words.ex_cn: 我们今天都穿了蓝色，真是巧合。
words.en: A coincidence is when two or more similar or related events occur at the same time by chance and without any planning.

words.tr:
n. 腐烂；衰落；
v. 腐烂；
words.ex: The fruit began to show signs of decay.
words.ex_cn: 这水果开始出现腐烂的迹象。
words.en: To decay means to be slowly destroyed by a natural process or to become gradually worse in quality, condition, or strength.

words.ex: The incidence of flu increased last winter.
words.ex_cn: 去年冬天流感的发生率上升了。
words.en: The incidence of something is the frequency with which it occurs or the rate at which it happens.

words.ex: I bought some milk, and incidentally, I saw your friend.
words.ex_cn: 我买了一些牛奶，顺便见到了你的朋友。
words.en: used to add something to what was said before, often something that you have just thought of

chapters.name: 词根 48. calc = stone 石头

words.ex: Milk has a lot of calcium.
words.ex_cn: 牛奶含有大量的钙。
words.en: A chemical element that is present in teeth and bones and is necessary for their health.

words.ex: He calculates the total cost quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他快速计算出总成本。
words.en: To determine by mathematical methods; compute.

words.tr: n. 微积分学；（人体内的）结石
words.ex: He is learning calculus at school.
words.ex_cn: 他正在学校学习微积分。
words.en: Calculus is a branch of mathematics that deals with the finding and properties of derivatives and integrals of functions, by methods originally based on the summation of infinitesimal differences.

chapters.name: 词根 49. calor = heat 热

words.ex: Bread and rice are rich in carbohydrate.
words.ex_cn: 面包和米饭富含碳水化合物。
words.en: A carbohydrate is a substance found in foods such as bread, potatoes, and rice which provides your body with heat and energy and which consists of carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen.

chapters.name: 词根 50. cand = white 白色的

words.ex: He is a candidate for the mayor position.
words.ex_cn: 他是市长职位的候选人。
words.en: A candidate is someone who is being considered for a position, for example someone who is running in an election or applying for a job.

chapters.name: 词根 51. cap, capt, cept, ceive, cip, cup = take, hold, seize 拿，抓，握住

words.ex: I anticipate rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我预料明天会下雨。
words.en: If you anticipate an event, you realize in advance that it may happen and you are prepared for it.

words.ex: He waited with anticipation for the results.
words.ex_cn: 他怀着期待等待结果。
words.en: Anticipation is a feeling of excitement about something pleasant or exciting that you know is going to happen.

words.ex: He is capable of solving hard math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他能解决复杂的数学问题。
words.en: If a person or thing is capable of doing something, they have the ability or potential to do it.

words.ex: He has the capacity to solve hard math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他有能力解决复杂的数学问题。
words.en: The capacity of a place or container is the amount of things or people that it can hold.

words.tr:
n. 插图说明；标题；字幕
v. 加上说明；加上标题；加上字幕
words.ex: The photo has a caption that says 'Happy birthday'.
words.ex_cn: 这张照片有一个标题，写着‘生日快乐’。
words.en: A caption is a short piece of text under a picture in a book, magazine, or newspaper that describes the picture or explains what is happening in it.

words.ex: The captive man sat quietly in his cell.
words.ex_cn: 那个被监禁的人安静地坐在牢房里。
words.en: A captive is someone who is being kept as a prisoner or in a confined space, or something that is held or confined.

words.ex: His conceit makes him ignore others' advice.
words.ex_cn: 他的自负让他忽视别人的建议。
words.en: An excessively favorable opinion of one's own abilities or worth; vanity.

words.tr: adj. 自负的；骄傲自大的
words.ex: He is conceited because he thinks he is the smartest.
words.ex_cn: 他自以为是，因为他觉得自己最聪明。
words.en: If you say that someone is conceited, you are showing your disapproval of the fact that they are far too proud of their abilities or achievements.

words.ex: His conceitedness made it hard for others to like him.
words.ex_cn: 他的自大让别人很难喜欢他。
words.en: The quality of being excessively proud of oneself; self-conceit.

words.ex: He could not conceive a world without technology.
words.ex_cn: 他无法设想一个没有科技的世界。
words.en: To conceive means to form or devise a plan or idea in the mind; to become pregnant.

words.ex: His conception of the new app was simple but clever.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个新应用的构想简单而巧妙。
words.en: A conception is an idea or a plan that someone has in their mind.

words.ex: The teacher explained the conceptual meaning of gravity.
words.ex_cn: 老师解释了重力的概念含义。
words.en: Relating to or based on mental concepts.

words.ex: His deceit made his friends lose trust in him.
words.ex_cn: 他的欺骗让朋友们失去了对他的信任。
words.en: Deceit is behaviour that is intended to make someone believe something that is not true.

words.ex: He deceived his friend with a lie.
words.ex_cn: 他用一个谎言欺骗了朋友。
words.en: If you deceive someone, you make them believe something that is not true, usually in order to get some advantage for yourself.

words.tr: adj. 卓越的；杰出的；罕见的；特别的；
words.ex: She is an exceptional student who always gets top grades.
words.ex_cn: 她是一名卓越的学生，总是取得最高分。
words.en: An exceptional person or thing has some unusual quality or ability that makes them different from others.

words.ex: The police intercepted the stolen car.
words.ex_cn: 警察拦截了那辆被盗的汽车。
words.en: If you intercept someone or something that is going from one place to another, you stop them before they get there.

words.tr: n. 中途夺取；拦截；侦听
words.ex: The player made an interception in the last minute.
words.ex_cn: 这名球员在最后一分钟完成了拦截。
words.en: The act of stopping and catching something that is in motion, especially a ball in sports or a message in communication.

words.tr: n. 拦截机；妨碍者；截击机；拦截者，拦截器
words.ex: The interceptor flew fast to catch the enemy plane.
words.ex_cn: 拦截机快速飞行以捕捉敌机。
words.en: An interceptor is a fast aircraft designed to stop or destroy enemy aircraft or missiles.

words.ex: The cat occupies the sofa all day.
words.ex_cn: 这只猫整天占据着沙发。
words.en: If people or things occupy a place, they are in it or fill it.

words.ex: The occupancy of the hotel is high during summer.
words.ex_cn: 夏天酒店的占用率很高。
words.en: The act of occupying or the state of being occupied, especially the condition of being occupied by tenants or the period during which a property is occupied.

words.ex: His perception of the sound was very sharp.
words.ex_cn: 他对声音的感知非常敏锐。
words.en: Your perception of something is the way that you think about it or the impression you have of it.

words.tr: adj. 观察敏锐的；有洞察力的
words.ex: She is perceptive and notices small changes.
words.ex_cn: 她很有洞察力，能注意到细微的变化。
words.en: If you describe someone as perceptive, you mean that they are good at noticing or understanding things.

words.tr: adj. 可察觉到的；看得出的；可感知的
words.ex: The change was barely perceptible.
words.ex_cn: 这个变化几乎无法察觉。
words.en: Something that is perceptible can be seen, noticed, or felt.

words.ex: He is principally responsible for the project.
words.ex_cn: 他主要负责这个项目。
words.en: Mainly; for the most part.

words.ex: He is the recipient of the prize.
words.ex_cn: 他是这个奖项的接受者。
words.en: A recipient is a person who receives something.

words.ex: Children are susceptible to colds.
words.ex_cn: 孩子容易感冒。
words.en: If you are susceptible to something or someone, you are very likely to be influenced by them.

words.ex: Children have higher susceptibility to colds.
words.ex_cn: 儿童更容易感冒。
words.en: The condition of being susceptible; the state of being easily affected, influenced, or harmed by something.

chapters.name: 词根 52. cap = head 头

words.ex: The lighthouse is on the cape.
words.ex_cn: 灯塔位于海角上。
words.en: A cape is a sleeveless outer garment that fastens at the neck and hangs over the shoulders and back, or a piece of land jutting into the sea or some other large body of water.

chapters.name: 词根 53. card, chart = paper 纸片

words.ex: The Magna Carta is an old charter of rights.
words.ex_cn: 《大宪章》是一份古老的权力宪章。
words.en: A charter is a formal document describing the rights, aims, or principles of an organization or group of people.

words.ex: He decided to discard his old habits.
words.ex_cn: 他决定抛开旧习惯。
words.en: To discard something means to get rid of it because you no longer want it or need it.

chapters.name: 词根 54. card, cord = heart 心脏

words.ex: The two countries signed an accord to stop the war.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家签署了一项协议以停止战争。
words.en: An accord is an official agreement or treaty. It can also refer to a state of agreement or harmony.

words.ex: The decision was made in accordance with the rules.
words.ex_cn: 这个决定是按照规则做出的。
words.en: Agreement or harmony; conformity.

words.tr:
adj. 首要的；大红色的
n. 红衣主教；枢机主教；基数
words.ex: This is a cardinal rule in our school.
words.ex_cn: 这是我们学校的一项首要规则。
words.en: A cardinal rule or quality is the most important one.

words.tr:
adj. 热诚的；友好的
n. 甜露酒
words.ex: He gave a cordial smile to his neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 他对着邻居露出了热情的微笑。
words.en: warm and friendly

words.ex: Their cordiality made everyone feel welcome.
words.ex_cn: 他们的友善让每个人都感到受欢迎。
words.en: Cordiality is behavior that is friendly and sincere.

words.ex: They had a discord about the movie ending.
words.ex_cn: 他们对电影的结局有分歧。
words.en: Disagreement or strife between people or groups.

chapters.name: 词根 55. cav = hole 洞

words.ex: The dentist found a cavity in his tooth.
words.ex_cn: 牙医在他的牙齿上发现了一个腔。
words.en: A cavity is a hole or space inside something.

chapters.name: 词根 56. ced(e), ceed, cess = go 行走

words.tr:
n. 接触（的机会或权利）；进入；通道；
v. 获取；使用；接近；
words.ex: Students need access to the library.
words.ex_cn: 学生需要有接触图书馆的机会。
words.en: If you have access to a building or other place, you are able to enter it or use it.

words.ex: He bought a new accessory for his phone.
words.ex_cn: 他为他的手机买了一个新配件。
words.en: An accessory is something such as a bag or piece of jewelry that you wear or carry because it is attractive.

words.tr: adj. 难以达到的；无法接近的；
words.ex: The mountain peak is inaccessible in winter.
words.ex_cn: 这座山峰在冬天难以到达。
words.en: If a place is inaccessible, it is very difficult or impossible to reach or enter.

words.ex: He finally conceded defeat after the match.
words.ex_cn: 比赛结束后，他终于承认失败了。
words.en: If you concede something, you admit, often unwillingly, that it is true or correct.

words.ex: He bought a concession ticket for the movie.
words.ex_cn: 他买了电影的减价票。
words.en: A concession is a point or principle that is granted or acknowledged in the course of an argument or negotiation, often as a compromise or to facilitate agreement.

words.tr: adj. 有妥协性的，让步的
words.ex: He passed the test, though he was tired.
words.ex_cn: 他虽然很累，但还是通过了考试。
words.en: A concessive clause or phrase is one that admits something that might be expected to contradict the main point of the sentence.

words.tr:
n. 过量；过度；超过；
adj. 多余的；
words.ex: The excess of sugar in his diet caused health problems.
words.ex_cn: 他饮食中糖分过量导致了健康问题。
words.en: An excess of something is a larger amount than is needed, allowed, or usual.

words.ex: He eats excessively sweets.
words.ex_cn: 他吃太多甜食。
words.en: To an excessive degree; more than is necessary, normal, or desirable; inordinately.

words.tr: n. 微处理器；微处理机
words.ex: The computer has a fast microprocessor.
words.ex_cn: 这台电脑有一个快速的微处理器。
words.en: A microprocessor is a small chip that can process data and carry out instructions in a computer or other electronic device.

words.ex: The rain precedes the storm.
words.ex_cn: 雨先于风暴来临。
words.en: If one event or period of time precedes another, it happens before it.

words.ex: The court followed the precedent set in 1995.
words.ex_cn: 法院遵循了1995年确立的先例。
words.en: A precedent is an action or decision that is used as an example when someone wants to do a similar thing in the future.

words.tr: v. 进行；继续；继续进行；“proceed”的现在分词；
words.ex: The meeting is proceeding as planned.
words.ex_cn: 会议按计划进行。
words.en: A proceeding is an event or a series of actions, especially one that is formal or official.

words.tr: n. 前任；前辈；原有事物
words.ex: He became the new manager, replacing his predecessor.
words.ex_cn: 他成为了新经理，接替了他的前任。
words.en: A predecessor is someone who had a job or a position before someone else, or something that comes before another thing in time or in a series.

words.tr: v. 后退；减弱；退出（某种活动）
words.ex: The flood waters begin to recede.
words.ex_cn: 洪水开始退去。
words.en: If something recedes, it becomes more distant or less noticeable.

words.tr:
n. 休息；休会；壁龛；壁凹
v. 放入壁龛；休息；休会
words.ex: The children play outside during recess.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在课间休息时到外面玩耍。
words.en: A recess is a break between the periods of work of an official body such as a committee, a court of law, or a government.

words.ex: Many people lost jobs during the recession.
words.ex_cn: 在经济不景气期间，许多人失去了工作。
words.en: A recession is a period when the economy of a country is not doing well, industrial production and business activity are at a low level, and many people are unemployed.

words.ex: The succession of rain made the ground wet.
words.ex_cn: 连续的雨水使地面变湿了。
words.en: A succession of things of the same kind is a number of them that exist or happen one after the other.

words.ex: The young manager is the successor to the CEO.
words.ex_cn: 这位年轻经理是首席执行官的接班人。
words.en: A successor is a person who takes a job or position previously held by someone else.

chapters.name: 词根 57. cel = elevate 提升

words.ex: He excels in math.
words.ex_cn: 他擅长数学。
words.en: To be exceptionally good at or proficient in an activity or subject.

chapters.name: 词根 58. celer = speed 速度

words.ex: The car will accelerate when you press the gas.
words.ex_cn: 当你踩油门时，汽车会加速。
words.en: To accelerate means to start to go faster or to make something start to go faster.

words.ex: The car's acceleration increased when the driver pressed the gas.
words.ex_cn: 当司机踩油门时，汽车的加速度增加了。
words.en: Acceleration is the rate at which a car or other vehicle can increase its speed, often measured in the time it takes to go from 0 to 60 miles per hour.

chapters.name: 词根 59. cem(e) = sleep 睡

words.ex: The old cemetery is near the church.
words.ex_cn: 那个古老的墓地在教堂附近。
words.en: A cemetery is a place where dead people are buried.

chapters.name: 词根 60. cens = judge 判断

words.tr:
n. 审查员；检查员
v. 检查；审查
words.ex: The censor removed the bad words from the movie.
words.ex_cn: 审查员从电影中删除了粗俗用语。
words.en: A censor is a person who supervises conduct and morals: in particular, one who examines books, films, or other material for objectionable matter.

words.ex: The government imposed censorship on the news.
words.ex_cn: 政府对新闻实施了审查。
words.en: Censorship is the censoring of books, plays, films, or reports, especially by government officials, because they are considered immoral or secret in some way.

words.ex: The government does a census every ten years.
words.ex_cn: 政府每十年进行一次人口普查。
words.en: A census is an official count or survey of a population, typically recording various details of individuals.

chapters.name: 词根 61. cent = sing 唱

words.ex: The bonus is an incentive to work harder.
words.ex_cn: 奖金是努力工作的动机。
words.en: Something that encourages a person to do something or to work harder.

chapters.name: 词根 62. centr = center 中心

words.ex: You must concentrate on your homework.
words.ex_cn: 你必须集中精力做作业。
words.en: If you concentrate on something, you give it your full attention and think about it carefully.

words.ex: He showed great concentration while solving the math problem.
words.ex_cn: 他在解这道数学题时非常专注。
words.en: Concentration is the ability to focus all your attention on one thing without being distracted.

words.ex: He is an eccentric man who wears socks with sandals.
words.ex_cn: 他是个古怪的人，穿着袜子配凉鞋。
words.en: If you say that someone is eccentric, you mean that they behave in a strange way, and have habits or opinions that are different from those of most people.

chapters.name: 词根 63. cere = grain 谷

words.ex: He eats cereal with milk every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上吃谷类食品配牛奶。
words.en: A cereal is a grass that is cultivated for the edible components of its grain, composed of the endosperm, germ, and bran.

chapters.name: 词根 64. cern, cert, cret = sure, separate 确定，区别

words.ex: The detective tried to ascertain the truth.
words.ex_cn: 侦探试图查明真相。
words.en: If you ascertain the truth about something, you find out what it is, especially by making a deliberate effort to do so.

words.tr: adj. 可查明的；可确定的
words.ex: The truth is ascertainable with enough evidence.
words.ex_cn: 有足够的证据时，真相是可以确定的。
words.en: Capable of being discovered or determined.

words.ex: The ascertainment of facts took a long time.
words.ex_cn: 事实的确认花了很长时间。
words.en: The act of finding something out or making sure of something.

words.tr:
n. 担忧；关注；
v. 涉及；
words.ex: His main concern is his child's safety.
words.ex_cn: 他主要的担忧是孩子的安全。
words.en: If something concerns you, it worries you or causes you to feel anxious.

words.ex: They made a concerted effort to clean the park.
words.ex_cn: 他们共同努力清理了公园。
words.en: A concerted action or effort is done by several people or groups working together.

words.ex: There is no certainty that it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 明天是否会下雨还没有确定。
words.en: Something that is certain is sure to happen or is definitely true.

words.ex: The doctor will certify that you are healthy.
words.ex_cn: 医生将证明你身体健康。
words.en: To officially declare something to be true, correct, or genuine, often in writing.

words.ex: He received a certificate for completing the course.
words.ex_cn: 他完成了课程后获得了证书。
words.en: A certificate is an official document attesting a fact, in particular.

words.ex: He could discern a small bird in the trees.
words.ex_cn: 他能辨明树上有一只小鸟。
words.en: If you can discern something, you are aware of it and know what it is.

words.ex: The difference is discernible to the naked eye.
words.ex_cn: 这个差异肉眼可见。
words.en: able to be discerned; perceptible

words.tr: adj. （言行）谨慎的；不显眼的；朴素的
words.ex: He was discreet about his personal life.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己的私生活很低调。
words.en: If you are discreet, you are polite and careful in what you do or say, because you want to avoid embarrassing or offending someone.

words.ex: The two groups are discrete and do not overlap.
words.ex_cn: 这两个群体是分离的，没有重叠。
words.en: Something that is discrete is separate and distinct in form or concept.

words.tr: n. 组件；不连续性（目标对于背景的显明度）
words.ex: The discreteness of the machine parts made assembly easier.
words.ex_cn: 机器零件的组件特性使组装更容易。
words.en: The quality of being individual and not divided or continuous.

chapters.name: 词根 65. cerpt = pluck 拔

words.tr:
n. 摘录；摘要
v. 摘录；引用
words.ex: He read an excerpt from the book.
words.ex_cn: 他读了这本书的一段摘录。
words.en: An excerpt is a short piece of writing or music which is taken from a larger piece.

chapters.name: 词根 66. chant = spell 咒语

words.tr: v. 使着迷；使陶醉；对…施魔法
words.ex: The magic show enchants the children.
words.ex_cn: 魔术表演让孩子们着迷。
words.en: If you are enchanted by someone or something, they cause you to have feelings of great delight or pleasure.

words.tr: adj. 迷人的；令人陶醉的； v. “enchant”的现在分词；
words.ex: The enchanting sunset made everyone stop and watch.
words.ex_cn: 迷人的日落让所有人都停下来看。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as enchanting, you mean that they are very attractive or charming.

chapters.name: 词根 67. cher = dear 可爱的

words.tr: v. 珍爱；爱惜；怀念；怀有（感情）；抱有（希望）
words.ex: I cherish the time I spend with my family.
words.ex_cn: 我珍惜与家人共度的时光。
words.en: If you cherish something, you care for it lovingly and protect it carefully.

chapters.name: 词根 68. chron = time 时间

words.ex: He has a chronic cough that lasts for months.
words.ex_cn: 他有一个持续数月的慢性咳嗽。
words.en: A chronic illness or condition lasts for a long time and cannot be cured, but it can usually be controlled.

chapters.name: 词根 69. chute = fall 降下

words.tr:
n. 降落伞
v. 跳伞；用降落伞空投
words.ex: He jumped from the plane and opened his parachute.
words.ex_cn: 他从飞机上跳下并打开了降落伞。
words.en: A parachute is a device used to slow the motion of an object through an atmosphere by creating drag.

words.ex: The parachutist jumped from the plane.
words.ex_cn: 跳伞者从飞机上跳下。
words.en: A parachutist is a person who jumps from an aircraft using a parachute.

chapters.name: 词根 70. cid, cis = cut, kill 切，杀

words.ex: He gave a concise answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了简明的回答。
words.en: Something that is concise says everything that is necessary without using any unnecessary words.

words.ex: He values conciseness in his writing.
words.ex_cn: 他重视写作的简洁性。
words.en: Conciseness refers to the quality of being concise, which means expressing what needs to be said without unnecessary words.

words.ex: He explained the idea concisely.
words.ex_cn: 他简洁地解释了这个想法。
words.en: In a concise manner; briefly and clearly.

words.ex: He felt so sad that he thought about suicide.
words.ex_cn: 他感到非常难过，以至于想到了自杀。
words.en: Suicide is the act of deliberately killing oneself.

words.tr: adv. 断然地；果断地；明确地；
words.ex: He decidedly refused to join the project.
words.ex_cn: 他断然拒绝参加这个项目。
words.en: In a way that is clear and definite; undoubtedly.

words.ex: His decisive action saved the team.
words.ex_cn: 他果断的行动拯救了团队。
words.en: If a fact, action, or event is decisive, it makes it certain that there will be a particular result.

words.ex: Farmers use pesticide to kill insects on crops.
words.ex_cn: 农民使用杀虫剂来杀死作物上的昆虫。
words.en: A pesticide is a chemical substance used to kill pests, especially insects, that damage crops or are harmful to human health.

chapters.name: 词根 71. cil = call 召集

words.ex: He tried to reconcile his work and family life.
words.ex_cn: 他试图调和工作与家庭生活。
words.en: If you reconcile two beliefs, facts, or demands that seem to be opposed or completely different, you find a way in which they can both be true or both be successful.

words.ex: The two friends reached reconciliation after talking for hours.
words.ex_cn: 两个朋友经过几个小时的交谈后和好了。
words.en: Reconciliation is the process of making two opposite beliefs, ideas, or situations agree.

chapters.name: 词根 72. circ, cycl = ring, circle 圆，环

words.tr: adj. 圆圈的；环形的；循环的；
words.ex: The table has a circular top.
words.ex_cn: 这张桌子有一个圆形的桌面。
words.en: Something that is circular is shaped like a circle.

words.tr: adj. 循环性的；促进循环的；（货币、报刊等）具有流通性的
words.ex: The circulative system moves blood through the body.
words.ex_cn: 循环系统将血液输送到全身。
words.en: Relating to or involved in circulation.

words.ex: The circulation of blood keeps us alive.
words.ex_cn: 血液的循环让我们活着。
words.en: The movement of something such as money or goods from place to place or from person to person; the number of copies of a newspaper or magazine that are sold.

words.ex: The children loved the circus with clowns and elephants.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们喜欢有小丑和大象的马戏团。
words.en: A circus is a group of performers that include clowns, acrobats, and trained animals, who travel to different places to entertain people.

words.ex: We recycle plastic bottles every week.
words.ex_cn: 我们每周回收塑料瓶。
words.en: To recycle means to process used materials so that they can be used again.

chapters.name: 词根 73. cite = quote, call 引用，唤起

words.ex: He cited a book in his essay.
words.ex_cn: 他在文章中引用了一本书。
words.en: To cite something means to quote it or mention it as evidence or proof of what you are saying.

words.ex: He gave a citation from the book.
words.ex_cn: 他引用了这本书中的一段话。
words.en: A citation is a reference to a published or unpublished source (not always the original source). More precisely, a citation is an abbreviated alphanumeric expression embedded in the body of an intellectual work that denotes an entry in the bibliographic references section of the work for the purpose of acknowledging the relevance of the works of others to the topic of discussion at the spot where the citation appears.

words.ex: He tried to incite a riot with his speech.
words.ex_cn: 他试图通过演讲煽动暴乱。
words.en: To incite someone to do something means to encourage or persuade them to do it, often in a way that is negative or harmful.

words.ex: His speech was called incitement to violence.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲被称为煽动暴力。
words.en: The act of encouraging someone to do something violent, illegal, or unpleasant, especially by making them angry or excited.

words.ex: The child recites the poem every morning.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子每天早上背诵这首诗。
words.en: To repeat aloud or declaim (a poem or passage) from memory before an audience.

chapters.name: 词根 74. civ = citizen 公民

words.ex: The civilian population stayed safe during the conflict.
words.ex_cn: 平民在冲突期间保持安全。
words.en: A civilian is a person who is not a member of the military or of a police or firefighting force.

chapters.name: 词根 75. claim, clam = cry, shout 喊叫

words.ex: The actor received acclaim for his performance.
words.ex_cn: 这位演员因他的表演而受到赞扬。
words.en: If someone or something is acclaimed, they are praised enthusiastically and publicly.

words.ex: He shouted an exclamation of surprise.
words.ex_cn: 他惊讶地喊了一声。
words.en: An exclamation is a sound, word, or sentence that is spoken suddenly, loudly, or emphatically and that expresses excitement, admiration, shock, or anger.

words.ex: The king proclaimed a new law.
words.ex_cn: 国王宣告了一项新法律。
words.en: If you proclaim something, you formally announce it or declare it publicly.

words.ex: The king made a proclamation about peace.
words.ex_cn: 国王发布了一项关于和平的公告。
words.en: A proclamation is a public announcement about something important, often made by a king, queen, or government.

words.tr: v. 要求归还；收回；开垦；感化
words.ex: He wants to reclaim his lost wallet.
words.ex_cn: 他想要要求归还他丢失的钱包。
words.en: If you reclaim something that you have lost or that has been taken away from you, you succeed in getting it back. If you reclaim land, you make it suitable for use, for example by draining it or by getting rid of unwanted buildings or plants.

words.tr: adj. 可收回的；可教化的
words.ex: The land is reclaimable with simple tools.
words.ex_cn: 这块土地用简单的工具就可以恢复利用。
words.en: Capable of being reclaimed; able to be recovered or reused.

words.tr: n. 开垦；土壤改良；改造；回收
words.ex: The city is doing reclamation of the old factory land.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市正在对旧工厂土地进行回收利用。
words.en: The process of claiming something back or of reasserting a right.

chapters.name: 词根 76. clar = clear 清楚，明白

words.ex: Can you clarify your answer?
words.ex_cn: 你能澄清一下你的答案吗？
words.en: To clarify something means to make it easier to understand by explaining it more clearly.

words.ex: The clarity of her explanation helped everyone understand.
words.ex_cn: 她解释的清晰帮助了每个人理解。
words.en: Clarity is the quality of being clear, in particular the quality of being easy to understand or see.

words.ex: The clearance of trash improved the park's appearance.
words.ex_cn: 清理垃圾改善了公园的外观。
words.en: Clearance refers to the process of removing or getting rid of something, or the space that is needed for one thing to move past another. It can also refer to the permission given for something to happen or be done.

words.ex: The country made a declaration of independence.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家发表了独立宣言。
words.en: A declaration is a formal statement or announcement.

chapters.name: 词根 77. clin, cliv = lean, slope 倾斜，斜坡

words.tr:
n. 下降；衰退；
v. 下降；衰退；
words.ex: There was a sharp decline in sales last month.
words.ex_cn: 上个月销售额大幅下降。
words.en: If something declines, it becomes less in quantity, importance, or strength.

words.tr: n. 倾斜；下倾；偏角；赤纬
words.ex: The sun's declination changes with the seasons.
words.ex_cn: 太阳的赤纬随季节变化。
words.en: The act of declining or a state of decline; a polite refusal; the angular distance of a celestial body north or south of the celestial equator.

words.ex: The road inclines sharply to the top of the hill.
words.ex_cn: 这条路陡峭地倾斜向山顶。
words.en: If you incline to a particular opinion, you have a tendency to think or behave in a particular way.

words.ex: He has an inclination to help others.
words.ex_cn: 他有帮助他人的倾向。
words.en: An inclination is a feeling that makes you want to act in a particular way, or a tendency to do something.

chapters.name: 词根 78. clos, clud, clus = close 关闭

words.tr:
n. 衣柜；壁橱；贮藏室
adj. 隐藏的
words.ex: He keeps his shirts in the closet.
words.ex_cn: 他把衬衫放在壁橱里。
words.en: A closet is a small room or space in a house or apartment where clothes, shoes, and other items are stored.

words.ex: He refused to disclose the secret.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝透露这个秘密。
words.en: To disclose information means to make it known to the public.

words.ex: The cows graze in the enclosure.
words.ex_cn: 奶牛在围场里吃草。
words.en: An enclosure is an area that is surrounded by a barrier or fence, often used to keep animals in or to protect something.

words.ex: This brand has an exclusive design.
words.ex_cn: 这个品牌拥有独有的设计。
words.en: Something that is exclusive is available only to particular people, and not to everyone.

words.tr: adj. 包容的；包含全部费用的；
words.ex: The school is inclusive and welcomes all students.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校是包容的，欢迎所有学生。
words.en: Inclusive is used to describe something that is designed to include all types of people, things, or ideas, and to treat them all fairly and equally.

words.ex: The inclusion of all students is important.
words.ex_cn: 包含所有学生是很重要的。
words.en: The act of including or the state of being included.

words.ex: The rain precludes a picnic.
words.ex_cn: 下雨阻止了野餐。
words.en: If something precludes an event or action, it prevents it from happening.

chapters.name: 词根 79. cogn = know 知道

words.ex: Children develop cognitive skills as they grow.
words.ex_cn: 孩子在成长过程中发展认知能力。
words.en: Cognitive means relating to the mental process involved in knowing, learning, and understanding things.

words.tr: n. 认可；识别；认识；承认；
words.ex: His hard work got recognition from his boss.
words.ex_cn: 他的努力得到了老板的认可。
words.en: The action or process of recognizing or being recognized, in particular.

chapters.name: 词根 80. colon = colony 殖民地

words.ex: The old house has a colonial style.
words.ex_cn: 这所老房子具有殖民地风格。
words.en: Colonial means relating to a system or period of colonization, or to the people who live in a colony.

words.tr: n. 殖民者；殖民地居民；移民
words.ex: The colonist built a small house near the river.
words.ex_cn: 这位殖民者在河边建了一座小房子。
words.en: A colonist is a person who settles in a new colony or moves to live in a new country.

words.ex: The country suffered under colonialism for many years.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家多年来遭受殖民主义的压迫。
words.en: Colonialism is the policy or practice of acquiring full or partial political control over another country, occupying it with settlers, and exploiting it economically.

chapters.name: 词根 81. com = banquet 宴会

words.tr:
n. 连环漫画；
adj. 滑稽的；
words.ex: He reads a comic every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上读一本连环漫画。
words.en: A comic is someone who entertains people by making them laugh, especially a professional comedian.

chapters.name: 词根 82. contra = opposite 相反

words.tr:
n. 对照；反差；对立；
v. 对比；和...形成对照；
words.ex: The contrast between light and dark is clear in the photo.
words.ex_cn: 这张照片中明暗的对照很明显。
words.en: A contrast is a great difference between two or more things which is clear when you compare them.

chapters.name: 词根 83. corpor = body 体

words.ex: The corporate office is in New York.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司的总部在纽约。
words.en: Corporate relates to large companies or to a particular large company.

words.ex: The new plan incorporates feedback from students.
words.ex_cn: 新计划包含了学生的反馈。
words.en: If one thing incorporates another thing, it includes the other thing.

words.ex: The incorporation of new ideas improved the plan.
words.ex_cn: 新想法的结合改进了这个计划。
words.en: Incorporation is the process or result of forming a legal corporation, or the inclusion of something as part of a whole.

words.tr: n. 合并者；法人创立者，[经管] 公司创办人
words.ex: He is the incorporator of the new company.
words.ex_cn: 他是这家新公司的发起人。
words.en: A person who forms a corporation or a company, or who is a member of a corporation.

chapters.name: 词根 84. cosm, cosmo = world 世界

words.ex: The cosmic rays come from outer space.
words.ex_cn: 宇宙射线来自外太空。
words.en: Relating to the universe or cosmos, especially as distinct from the earth.

words.ex: He loves to watch the cosmos at night.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢在夜晚观看宇宙。
words.en: The cosmos refers to the universe seen as a well-ordered whole, or to any system or structure that is complex and orderly.

words.ex: He believes in cosmism, that everything is connected in the universe.
words.ex_cn: 他相信宇宙主义，认为宇宙中的一切都是相互联系的。
words.en: Cosmism is a philosophical and cultural movement that views the cosmos as a living, interconnected entity with intrinsic value and purpose.

chapters.name: 词根 85. cour, cours, cur, curs = run 跑

words.ex: He tried to curb his horse with the reins.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用缰绳勒住马。
words.en: If you curb something, you control it and keep it within limits.

words.ex: The currency in Japan is the yen.
words.ex_cn: 日本的货币是日元。
words.en: The system of money in general use in a particular country.

words.ex: She is currently working at a hospital.
words.ex_cn: 她目前正在一家医院工作。
words.en: at the present time

words.tr:
adj. 当前的；流通的；
n. （水、气、电）流；趋势；
words.ex: The current weather is very hot.
words.ex_cn: 当前的天气非常热。
words.en: belonging to the present time; happening or being used or done now

words.ex: The course of the river changed after the flood.
words.ex_cn: 河流的流程在洪水后发生了变化。
words.en: A course is a series of lessons or lectures on a particular subject.

words.ex: His discourse on climate change was clear and logical.
words.ex_cn: 他关于气候变化的论述清晰而有逻辑。
words.en: Discourse is spoken or written communication between people, especially serious discussion of a particular subject.

words.ex: We went on an excursion to the mountains last weekend.
words.ex_cn: 上周末我们去山区进行了短途旅行。
words.en: An excursion is a short journey or trip, especially one taken as a leisure activity.

words.ex: He incurred a fine for speeding.
words.ex_cn: 他因超速而招致了一笔罚款。
words.en: If you incur something unpleasant, it happens to you because of something you have done.

words.ex: There is little intercourse between the two villages.
words.ex_cn: 这两个村庄之间很少交往。
words.en: Intercourse refers to communication or dealings between individuals or groups, or sexual activity between people.

words.ex: The occurrence of rain surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 下雨这件事让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: An occurrence is something that happens or takes place.

words.ex: The problem recurs every week.
words.ex_cn: 这个问题每周都会再次出现。
words.en: If something recurs, it happens again, either once or several times.

words.ex: The recurrence of storms caused many problems.
words.ex_cn: 风暴的反复出现造成了许多问题。
words.en: The return of a sign, symptom, or disease after a remission.

chapters.name: 词根 86. court = polite 礼貌的

words.ex: He was courteous to everyone he met.
words.ex_cn: 他对遇到的每个人都很有礼貌。
words.en: Someone who is courteous is polite and respectful to other people.

words.ex: He showed courtesy by holding the door open.
words.ex_cn: 他为别人扶着门，表现得很礼貌。
words.en: Courtesy is polite behavior, or a polite action or remark.

chapters.name: 词根 87. cow = scare 吓唬

words.tr:
n. 懦夫；胆小鬼；胆怯者
adj. 胆小的；怯懦的
words.ex: He was a coward and ran away from the fight.
words.ex_cn: 他是个懦夫，逃跑了。
words.en: A coward is someone who is easily frightened and avoids dangerous or difficult situations.

words.tr:
adj. 怯懦的；胆小的
adv. 胆怯地
words.ex: He was cowardly and ran away from the fight.
words.ex_cn: 他很懦弱，逃跑了。
words.en: If you describe someone as cowardly, you disapprove of them because they are easily frightened and avoid dangerous or difficult situations.

chapters.name: 词根 88. cracy = rule 统治

words.tr: n. 官僚主义；官僚机构
words.ex: He hates the bureaucracy in government offices.
words.ex_cn: 他讨厌政府办公室里的官僚主义。
words.en: Bureaucracy refers to a system of government or business that has many complicated rules and ways of doing things.

words.tr: adj. 官僚的；官僚主义的；
words.ex: The bureaucratic process made it hard to get a permit.
words.ex_cn: 官僚程序让申请许可证变得困难。
words.en: If you describe a system, organization, or process as bureaucratic, you mean that it is complicated and inefficient because of a large number of rules and procedures.

words.tr: n. 官僚主义；官僚作风
words.ex: Bureaucratism slows down the process of getting permits.
words.ex_cn: 官僚主义拖慢了获取许可证的进程。
words.en: Bureaucratism refers to the excessive adherence to formal rules and procedures in the administration of a country or organization, often leading to inefficiency and a lack of responsiveness to the needs of the people.

chapters.name: 词根 89. cramb = crawl 爬

words.ex: There was a scramble for the last ticket.
words.ex_cn: 大家争相抢购最后一张票。
words.en: If you scramble over rocks or up a hill, you move quickly over them or up it using your hands to help you. Scramble can also mean to compete or struggle with others for something that is in short supply.

chapters.name: 词根 90. cre = grow 增长

words.ex: The painting is a beautiful creation of the artist.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画是艺术家的一个美丽作品。
words.en: The act or process of bringing something into existence.

words.ex: He is a creative boy who draws nice pictures.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个有创造力的男孩，会画漂亮的画。
words.en: Someone who is creative has the ability to invent and develop original ideas, especially in the arts.

words.tr: n. 娱乐；消遣；休闲活动
words.ex: Reading books is his favorite recreation.
words.ex_cn: 读书是他最喜欢的消遣。
words.en: Recreation is activity that you do for enjoyment or amusement when you are not working.

chapters.name: 词根 91. cred = believe 相信

words.tr:
n. 信用；赊账；赞扬；贷款；荣誉；
v. 相信；
words.ex: He has good credit with the bank.
words.ex_cn: 他在银行有良好的信用。
words.en: If you are allowed credit, you are allowed to pay for goods or services several weeks or months after you have received them.

words.ex: The movie was incredible.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影太棒了。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as incredible, you like them very much or are impressed by them, because they are extremely or unusually good.

words.ex: The witness lost credibility after lying.
words.ex_cn: 证人因撒谎而失去了可信性。
words.en: The quality of being trusted and believed in.

chapters.name: 词根 92. crep = break 破裂

words.ex: There is a discrepancy between the two reports.
words.ex_cn: 这两份报告之间有差异。
words.en: A discrepancy is a difference between two or more things that should be the same.

chapters.name: 词根 93. crimin = discern 识别

words.ex: They discriminate against people because of their race.
words.ex_cn: 他们因为种族而歧视他人。
words.en: To discriminate means to recognize a distinction; differentiate. It can also mean to make an unjust or prejudicial distinction in the treatment of different categories of people, especially on the grounds of race, sex, or age.

words.ex: He noticed the discrimination between the two prices.
words.ex_cn: 他注意到了两个价格之间的区别。
words.en: The unjust or prejudicial treatment of different categories of people, especially on the grounds of race, age, or sex.

chapters.name: 词根 94. crit = judge 判断

words.ex: The main criterion for winning is fairness.
words.ex_cn: 获胜的主要标准是公平。
words.en: A criterion is a principle or standard by which something may be judged or decided.

words.tr: adj. 至关重要的；批判性的；关键的；危急的；临界的；
words.ex: Water is critical for life.
words.ex_cn: 水对生命至关重要。
words.en: If you are critical of someone or something, you show that you disapprove of them. In a critical situation, things are very serious and dangerous. A critical time or event is extremely important because it will affect future events.

words.ex: He often criticizes his brother for being late.
words.ex_cn: 他经常批评他弟弟迟到。
words.en: If you criticize someone or something, you express your disapproval of them by saying what you think is wrong with them.

chapters.name: 词根 95. cru = cross 交叉

words.tr:
n. 乘船游览；航游；
v. 乘船游览；航游；
words.ex: We went on a cruise around the Mediterranean Sea.
words.ex_cn: 我们乘船游览了地中海。
words.en: To sail about in an area without a precise destination, especially for pleasure.

words.ex: The cruiser sailed slowly across the ocean.
words.ex_cn: 巡洋舰缓缓驶过海洋。
words.en: A cruiser is a large fast warship, or a large motorboat used for pleasure trips.

chapters.name: 词根 96. culmin = top 顶

words.tr: v. 到达…的顶点；达到高潮；告终
words.ex: The concert culminated with a loud fireworks show.
words.ex_cn: 音乐会以一场响亮的烟花表演结束。
words.en: If an event or series of events culminates in something, it ends with it, having developed until it reaches this point.

words.ex: The concert was the culmination of his music career.
words.ex_cn: 这场音乐会是他音乐生涯的顶点。
words.en: The culmination of something is the highest or final point of it, often after a long period of development.

chapters.name: 词根 97. cumul = heap 堆积

words.ex: He accumulates coins from different countries.
words.ex_cn: 他收集来自不同国家的硬币。
words.en: To accumulate means to gradually gather or acquire an increasing number or quantity of something.

words.ex: The cumulative score is the total of all previous points.
words.ex_cn: 累积得分是所有之前分数的总和。
words.en: If a series of events have a cumulative effect, each event makes the effect greater.

chapters.name: 词根 98. cur = care 关心

words.tr: adj. 不精确的；不准确的；有错误的；
words.ex: The clock is inaccurate and shows the wrong time.
words.ex_cn: 这个钟不精确，显示的时间不对。
words.en: If a statement or measurement is inaccurate, it is not correct or not exact.

words.tr: n. 不准确；不精确；错误
words.ex: The inaccuracy of the clock caused delays.
words.ex_cn: 钟的不准确导致了延误。
words.en: The quality or state of being inaccurate; error.

words.ex: The meaning of the poem is obscure.
words.ex_cn: 这首诗的意思不清楚。
words.en: If something is obscure, it is not well known or not easily understood.

chapters.name: 词根 99. custom = habit 习惯

words.ex: It is customary to shake hands when you meet someone.
words.ex_cn: 见面时握手是习惯做法。
words.en: Something that is customary is normal because it is the way something is usually done.

chapters.name: 词根 100. cylind = roll 卷

words.ex: The engine has four cylinders.
words.ex_cn: 发动机有四个气缸。
words.en: A cylinder is a geometric figure with straight parallel sides and a circular or oval cross section.

words.tr: adj. 圆柱形的；圆筒状的；
words.ex: The glass has a cylindrical shape.
words.ex_cn: 这个玻璃杯是圆柱形的。
words.en: Something that is cylindrical is in the shape of a cylinder.

chapters.name: 词根 101. de = leave 离开

words.ex: The boy defied his parents by staying out late.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩因为熬夜不回家而违抗了父母。
words.en: If you defy someone or something, you refuse to obey them or you do something that they do not allow.

words.ex: The boy showed defiance by refusing to follow the rules.
words.ex_cn: 男孩通过拒绝遵守规则来表现违抗。
words.en: Defiance is behaviour or an attitude which shows that you are not willing to obey someone or something.

chapters.name: 词根 102. deavor = duty 职责

words.tr:
n. 尽力；尝试；
v. 尽力；奋力；
words.ex: His endeavor to finish the project took all his energy.
words.ex_cn: 他为完成这个项目付出了全部努力。
words.en: An endeavor is an attempt to do something, especially something new or original.

chapters.name: 词根 103. dec = ten 十

words.tr:
adj. 小数的；十进位的
n. 小数
words.ex: The decimal point separates the whole number from the decimal part.
words.ex_cn: 小数点将整数部分与小数部分分开。
words.en: A decimal is a fraction that is written in a special form. It is based on powers of ten, and it uses a decimal point to separate the whole number part from the fractional part.

words.ex: The country completed decimalization in 1971.
words.ex_cn: 该国在1971年完成了十进制化。
words.en: The process of changing a system of currency or measurement to a decimal system.

chapters.name: 词根 104. decor = ornament 装饰

words.tr: adj. 装饰性的；作装饰用的；
words.ex: The room has decorative flowers on the table.
words.ex_cn: 房间里桌上有一些装饰性的花。
words.en: Something that is decorative is intended to look pretty or attractive.

chapters.name: 词根 105. dem, demo = people 人们

words.ex: The epidemic spread quickly across the country.
words.ex_cn: 这种流行病迅速蔓延到全国。
words.en: An epidemic is a large number of cases of an infectious disease occurring at the same time.

chapters.name: 词根 106. demn = harm 伤害

words.ex: The public condemned the corrupt politician.
words.ex_cn: 公众谴责了这位腐败的政客。
words.en: If you condemn something, you say that it is very bad and unacceptable.

words.ex: The public expressed condemnation for the violent act.
words.ex_cn: 公众对这一暴力行为表示谴责。
words.en: Condemnation is the act of saying that something or someone is very bad and unacceptable.

chapters.name: 词根 107. dent = tooth 牙齿

words.ex: He visits the dentist every six months.
words.ex_cn: 他每六个月去看一次牙医。
words.en: A dentist is a person who is qualified to treat diseases and conditions that affect the teeth and gums, especially the repair and extraction of teeth and the insertion of artificial ones.

words.ex: He wants to study dentistry after high school.
words.ex_cn: 他想在高中毕业后学习牙科。
words.en: Dentistry is the profession or science concerned with the prevention and treatment of diseases and disorders of the teeth and gums.

chapters.name: 词根 108. desir = want 渴望

words.tr: adj. 不合意的；不想要的；
words.ex: The weather is undesirable for a picnic.
words.ex_cn: 这种天气不适合野餐。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as undesirable, you think they will have harmful effects or cause problems.

chapters.name: 词根 109. deterior = worse 更坏

words.ex: The weather will deteriorate tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 明天天气会恶化。
words.en: If something deteriorates, it becomes worse in some way.

words.ex: The deterioration of the road made driving dangerous.
words.ex_cn: 道路的恶化使驾驶变得危险。
words.en: The process of becoming progressively worse.

chapters.name: 词根 110. dic, dict = say 言，说

words.ex: He is an addict who cannot stop smoking.
words.ex_cn: 他是个无法戒烟的瘾君子。
words.en: An addict is someone who is unable to stop taking harmful drugs, or someone who is very interested in something and spends a lot of time doing it.

words.ex: He contradicts what she said.
words.ex_cn: 他反驳了她的话。
words.en: If you contradict someone, you say that what they have just said is wrong, or you suggest that it is wrong by saying something different.

words.ex: His words were contradictory.
words.ex_cn: 他的话是矛盾的。
words.en: If two or more facts, ideas, or statements are contradictory, they state or imply that opposite things are true.

words.ex: His words are a contradiction.
words.ex_cn: 他的话是矛盾的。
words.en: A contradiction is a situation or statement in which two aspects or elements are opposed to each other, making it impossible for both to be true at the same time.

words.ex: He dedicates his time to helping poor children.
words.ex_cn: 他致力于帮助贫困儿童。
words.en: If you dedicate yourself to something, you give all your attention and effort to it.

words.ex: The dictator ruled the country for many years.
words.ex_cn: 这位独裁者统治这个国家很多年。
words.en: A dictator is a ruler who has complete power in a country, especially when this power has been obtained by force and is used unfairly or cruelly.

words.ex: The boss is dictatorial and never listens to others.
words.ex_cn: 老板很专横，从不听别人的意见。
words.en: If you describe someone as dictatorial, you are criticizing them for behaving in a way that shows they expect to be obeyed without question.

words.ex: The dark clouds are an indication of rain.
words.ex_cn: 乌云是下雨的迹象。
words.en: An indication is a sign which suggests, for example, what people are thinking or feeling.

words.ex: The map has an indicative arrow to show the way.
words.ex_cn: 这张地图上有一个指示方向的箭头。
words.en: If one thing is indicative of another, it suggests what the other thing is likely to be.

words.ex: The old woman predict rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 那位老妇人预言明天会下雨。
words.en: If you predict an event, you say that it will happen.

words.ex: The weather prediction says it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 天气预测说明天会下雨。
words.en: A prediction is a statement about what you think will happen in the future.

words.ex: The weather was predictable today, just like yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 今天的天气和昨天一样，是可以预见的。
words.en: If you say that an event or a situation is predictable, you mean that it is obvious in advance that it will happen or what it will be like.

words.ex: The model gives predictive results for next month's sales.
words.ex_cn: 这个模型提供了下个月销售额的预测结果。
words.en: If you use predictive to describe something, you mean that it is able to predict what will happen in the future.

chapters.name: 词根 111. dign = noble 高贵

words.ex: He kept his dignity even when he was poor.
words.ex_cn: 即使他很穷，他依然保持尊严。
words.en: Dignity is the quality of being worthy of honor or respect.

words.tr: v. 使有尊严；使崇高；使显贵
words.ex: He tried to dignify his actions with excuses.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用借口来美化自己的行为。
words.en: To dignify something means to make it seem important and worthy of respect, often by treating it in a serious or formal way.

words.ex: He felt indignant when they blamed him for the mistake.
words.ex_cn: 当他们把错误归咎于他时，他感到愤愤不平。
words.en: If you are indignant, you are shocked and angry, because you think that something is unjust or unfair.

words.ex: He felt indignation when he saw the unfair rule.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到不公平的规则时，他感到愤怒。
words.en: Indignation is a feeling of anger and surprise which you have when you think that something is wrong or unfair.

chapters.name: 词根 112. doc, doct = teach 教

words.tr:
n. 纪录片；
adj. 文书的；
words.ex: We watched a documentary about pandas last night.
words.ex_cn: 我们昨晚看了一部关于熊猫的纪录片。
words.en: A documentary is a film or television or radio programme that gives factual information about a particular subject.

words.ex: The church teaches its doctrine to all members.
words.ex_cn: 教会向所有成员传授它的教义。
words.en: A doctrine is a set of beliefs or principles that are taught or accepted by a particular group, especially in religion or politics.

chapters.name: 词根 113. dom = house 屋，家

words.ex: The church has a big dome above the altar.
words.ex_cn: 教堂的祭坛上方有一个大穹顶。
words.en: A dome is a rounded vault made of either curved segments or a shell of revolution, meaning an arch rotated around its central vertical axis.

words.tr: adj. 圆屋顶的；穹窿式的
words.ex: The dome has a domical shape.
words.ex_cn: 这个圆顶具有穹顶形状。
words.en: Relating to or resembling a dome.

words.tr: adj. 家庭的；国内的；驯养的；
words.ex: She prefers domestic chores over going out.
words.ex_cn: 她更喜欢做家务而不是外出。
words.en: Domestic means relating to the home, family, or household affairs. It can also refer to something that is made or produced within a country and not imported.

chapters.name: 词根 114. don = give 给予

words.ex: He donate money to the poor children.
words.ex_cn: 他向贫困儿童捐赠钱。
words.en: To donate means to give something, especially money, to a person or organization that needs help.

words.ex: The hospital received a donation of books.
words.ex_cn: 医院收到了一批书籍捐赠。
words.en: A donation is a gift which is given to a charity or other organization.

chapters.name: 词根 115. doub, du, dub = two 二，双

words.ex: He is doubtless the best player on the team.
words.ex_cn: 他无疑是队里最好的球员。
words.en: used to say that something is almost certain or very likely

words.tr: v. 复制；复印；再做一次；
words.ex: He duplicated the file to save a copy.
words.ex_cn: 他复制了该文件以保存一份副本。
words.en: To duplicate something means to make an exact copy of it.

words.ex: The duplication of the document cost five dollars.
words.ex_cn: 这份文件的复制花了五美元。
words.en: the act or process of making an exact copy of something

words.ex: He has a dual role as teacher and coach.
words.ex_cn: 他同时担任老师和教练的双重角色。
words.en: Having two parts or aspects.

words.tr: v. 起绰号；把…称作；配音；译制
words.ex: They dubbed him 'Captain Cool' for his calm style.
words.ex_cn: 他们因为他冷静的风格给他起了个绰号叫‘冷静队长’。
words.en: To give a name, title, or nickname to someone or something; to provide a film or television program with a soundtrack in a different language from the original.

words.tr: adj. 可疑的；怀疑的；拿不准的；
words.ex: The deal seemed dubious to me.
words.ex_cn: 这个交易在我看来很可疑。
words.en: If you describe something as dubious, you mean that you do not consider it to be completely honest, safe, or reliable.

chapters.name: 词根 116. dox = opinion 观点

words.ex: He follows the orthodox religious practices.
words.ex_cn: 他遵循正统的宗教习俗。
words.en: Orthodox beliefs, methods, or systems are ones which are accepted or used by most people.

words.ex: It's a paradox that he is rich but unhappy.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个悖论，他很富有却不快乐。
words.en: A paradox is a statement that seems to contradict itself but may nonetheless be true, or a situation that defies intuition.

chapters.name: 词根 117. dra = perform 表演

words.ex: The company made drastic cuts to save money.
words.ex_cn: 公司进行了急剧的削减以节省资金。
words.en: If you describe a change or action as drastic, you mean that it is extreme and often severe.

chapters.name: 词根 118. drom = run 跑

words.tr: n. 综合征；综合症状；典型表现；
words.ex: He was diagnosed with sleep apnea syndrome.
words.ex_cn: 他被诊断出患有睡眠呼吸暂停综合征。
words.en: A syndrome is a set of medical signs and symptoms which are correlated with each other and often associated with a particular disease or disorder.

chapters.name: 词根 119. duc, duct = lead 引导

words.ex: The factory makes cheese, and whey is a by-product.
words.ex_cn: 这家工厂生产奶酪，乳清是副产品。
words.en: A by-product is something that is produced as a result of making something else, or something unexpected that happens as a result of something.

words.tr: adj. 富有成效的；多产的；生产的；
words.ex: He had a productive day and finished all his work.
words.ex_cn: 他度过了富有成效的一天，完成了所有工作。
words.en: Producing or able to produce large amounts of goods, crops, or other commodities.

words.ex: The factory improved its productivity by using new machines.
words.ex_cn: 工厂通过使用新机器提高了生产率。
words.en: Productivity is the rate at which goods are produced or work is completed.

words.ex: The reproduction of rabbits is very fast.
words.ex_cn: 兔子的生殖速度很快。
words.en: The process of producing offspring or new individuals of the same species, or the act of making a copy of something.

words.tr:
v. 实施；传导（电、热）；
n. 行为；举止；
words.ex: The company will conduct a survey next week.
words.ex_cn: 公司将在下周进行一项调查。
words.en: To organize and carry out a particular activity.

words.ex: He can deduce the answer from the clues.
words.ex_cn: 他能从线索中推断出答案。
words.en: If you deduce something or deduce that something is true, you reach that conclusion because of other things that you know to be true.

words.ex: He uses deductive reasoning to solve the puzzle.
words.ex_cn: 他使用演绎推理来解决这个谜题。
words.en: Deductive reasoning is a logical process in which a conclusion is based on the concordance of multiple premises that are generally assumed to be true.

words.ex: He deducts tax from his salary every month.
words.ex_cn: 他每月从工资中扣除税款。
words.en: If you deduct an amount from a total, you subtract it from the total.

words.ex: His deduction was based on the evidence.
words.ex_cn: 他的推论基于证据。
words.en: A deduction is a conclusion that you reach about something because of other things that you know to be true.

words.ex: The ad induced him to buy the product.
words.ex_cn: 这则广告诱使他购买了该产品。
words.en: To induce a state or condition means to cause it.

words.ex: He accepted the job because of the financial inducement.
words.ex_cn: 他因为经济诱因接受了这份工作。
words.en: Something that is offered to someone to persuade them to do something.

words.ex: The induction of the new mayor will be held next Monday.
words.ex_cn: 新市长的就职典礼将在下周一举行。
words.en: Induction is the process or action of inducting someone to a position or organization, or the process of reasoning from specific cases to general rules.

chapters.name: 词根 120. due = withdraw 退回

words.ex: The police tried to subdue the angry man.
words.ex_cn: 警察试图制服那个愤怒的人。
words.en: To subdue someone or something means to bring them under control by using force or persuasion.

words.tr: adj. 可征服的；可抑制的
words.ex: The wild dog was subduable with patience.
words.ex_cn: 这只野狗通过耐心是可以被制服的。
words.en: Capable of being subdued or conquered.

chapters.name: 词根 121. dur = last 持久

words.ex: He built his endurance by running every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他通过每天早晨跑步来增强耐力。
words.en: The ability to endure an unpleasant or difficult process or situation without giving up.

words.ex: He had to endure the cold winter without a coat.
words.ex_cn: 他不得不在没有外套的情况下忍受寒冷的冬天。
words.en: To endure means to suffer something difficult, unpleasant, or painful, or to continue to exist for a long time.

words.ex: The pain was endurable, so she kept going.
words.ex_cn: 疼痛是可以忍受的，所以她继续前行。
words.en: If something is endurable, it is possible to be tolerated or endured.

chapters.name: 词根 122. dynam = power 力量

words.tr:
adj. 动态的；有活力的；不断变化的；
n. 活力；动力；
words.ex: The game has dynamic weather that changes every hour.
words.ex_cn: 这个游戏有每小时变化的动态天气。
words.en: If you describe someone as dynamic, you approve of them because they are full of energy or full of new ideas.

words.ex: The old factory uses a dynamo to produce electricity.
words.ex_cn: 这家老工厂使用一台发电机来发电。
words.en: A dynamo is a device for converting mechanical energy into electrical energy, typically by rotating coils of copper wire in a magnetic field.

chapters.name: 词根 123. eco = environment 环境，生态

words.ex: He studies ecology to understand how animals live with plants.
words.ex_cn: 他学习生态学以了解动物如何与植物共存。
words.en: Ecology is the study of the relationships between living organisms, including humans, and their physical environment; it seeks to understand the vital connections between plants and animals and the world around them.

words.ex: This park is an ecological habitat for many birds.
words.ex_cn: 这个公园是许多鸟类的生态栖息地。
words.en: Relating to or concerned with the relation of living organisms to one another and to their physical surroundings.

words.tr: n. 生态学家；生态学者；
words.ex: The ecologist studied birds in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 这位生态学家研究了森林里的鸟类。
words.en: An ecologist is a scientist who studies the relationships between living things and their environment.

chapters.name: 词根 124. econom = economy 经济

words.tr: adv. 跟经济有关地；经济地；
words.ex: The country is developing economically.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家正在经济上发展。
words.en: In a way that relates to economics or finance; in a way that uses no more of something than is necessary.

words.ex: He majors in economics at university.
words.ex_cn: 他在大学主修经济学。
words.en: Economics is the study of the way in which money, industry, and trade are organized in a society.

chapters.name: 词根 125. ed = eat 吃

words.tr: adj. 可食用的；可以吃的；
words.ex: These mushrooms are edible and safe to eat.
words.ex_cn: 这些蘑菇是可食用的，安全可以吃。
words.en: Fit to be eaten as food.

chapters.name: 词根 126. eg = I 我

words.ex: He has a big ego and likes to show off.
words.ex_cn: 他自尊心很强，喜欢炫耀。
words.en: Your ego is your opinion of your own worth. For example, if someone has a big ego, they think they are very important and valuable.

words.tr: n. 自我主义；利己主义
words.ex: He acts out of egoism, not kindness.
words.ex_cn: 他出于利己主义行事，而不是善意。
words.en: Egoism is the belief that you should think about your own interests and needs rather than those of other people.

words.tr: n. 自我主义者；利己主义者
words.ex: He is an egoist who only thinks about himself.
words.ex_cn: 他是个只为自己着想的利己主义者。
words.en: An egoist is someone who is excessively self-centered and selfish, often disregarding the needs and feelings of others.

chapters.name: 词根 127. electr = electricity 电

words.ex: The electrician fixed the broken light.
words.ex_cn: 电工修好了坏掉的灯。
