words.en: To stabilize something means to make it stable or to prevent it from changing or declining.

words.ex: The stabilization of the economy took many years.
words.ex_cn: 经济的稳定花了许多年。
words.en: The process of making something physically stable or the act of stabilizing the economy or a patient's condition.

words.ex: The chair is stationary and does not move.
words.ex_cn: 这把椅子是固定的，不会移动。
words.en: not moving or not intended to be moved

words.ex: The statistics show a rise in sales last year.
words.ex_cn: 这些统计数字显示去年销售额有所上升。
words.en: Statistics is a branch of mathematics dealing with the collection, analysis, interpretation, presentation, and organization of data.

words.ex: Water is a common substance.
words.ex_cn: 水是一种常见的物质。
words.en: A substance is a particular kind of matter with uniform properties.

words.tr: adj. 大量的；重大的；实质性的；
words.ex: He made a substantial profit from the sale.
words.ex_cn: 他从这次销售中获得了大量的利润。
words.en: Something that is substantial is large in size, amount, or importance.

words.tr: adj. 本质上的；实质性的；
words.ex: The change was substantive, not just cosmetic.
words.ex_cn: 这个改变是本质上的，而不仅仅是表面上的。
words.en: Something that is substantive is significant, meaningful, or important in a way that is not just superficial or formal.

chapters.name: 词根 445. stall = place 放

words.ex: He paid the first installment last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周支付了第一期分期付款。
words.en: An installment is one of the amounts, usually equal, into which a debt is divided for payment at stated intervals over a fixed period.

chapters.name: 词根 446. stereo = solid 固体的

words.tr:
n. 刻板印象；陈规老套
v. 对…存有成见；把…模式化
words.ex: He broke the stereotype that boys cannot cry.
words.ex_cn: 他打破了男孩不能哭的刻板印象。
words.en: A stereotype is a fixed general image or set of characteristics that a lot of people believe represent a particular type of person or thing.

chapters.name: 词根 447. still = small drop 小水滴

words.tr: v. 蒸馏；用蒸馏法提取；蒸馏出；提炼
words.ex: They distill water to remove impurities.
words.ex_cn: 他们通过蒸馏去除水中的杂质。
words.en: To distill a liquid means to purify it by heating it until it becomes a gas and then cooling it so that it becomes a liquid again. This process can also be used to extract the essential elements or meanings from something.

words.ex: The distillation of water removes impurities.
words.ex_cn: 水的蒸馏过程可以去除杂质。
words.en: The process of purifying a liquid by heating it until it becomes a vapor and then cooling the vapor to collect the purified liquid.

chapters.name: 词根 448. sting, stinct = prick 刺，刺激

words.ex: The two colors are distinct.
words.ex_cn: 这两种颜色有区别。
words.en: If something is distinct, it is easily seen, heard, or understood.

words.tr: n. 区别；区分；优等评分；
words.ex: There is a clear distinction between right and wrong.
words.ex_cn: 对与错之间有明显的区别。
words.en: A distinction is a difference or contrast between similar things or people.

words.ex: The two colors distinguish the two teams.
words.ex_cn: 这两种颜色使两个队伍有所不同。
words.en: If you can distinguish one thing from another, you can see or understand how they are different.

words.tr: adj. 灭绝的；熄灭的；绝种的；
words.ex: The dodo is an extinct bird.
words.ex_cn: 渡渡鸟是一种灭绝的鸟。
words.en: If a species of animals or plants is extinct, it no longer has any living members, either in the world or in a particular place.

words.ex: The extinction of dinosaurs happened millions of years ago.
words.ex_cn: 恐龙的灭绝发生在数百万年前。
words.en: The state or process of a species, family, or larger group being or becoming extinct.

words.ex: He extinguished the fire with water.
words.ex_cn: 他用水把火扑灭了。
words.en: To extinguish a fire or a light means to stop it burning or shining.

words.ex: He picked up the fire extinguisher to put out the flames.
words.ex_cn: 他拿起灭火器来扑灭火焰。
words.en: An extinguisher is a device that is used to put out fires.

words.ex: She tied the box with a thin string.
words.ex_cn: 她用一根细线把盒子绑了起来。
words.en: A string is a thin piece of rope or cord, or a series of things connected together.

chapters.name: 词根 449. stit, stitut = set up, place 建立，放

words.tr:
n. 成分；
adj. 构成的；
words.ex: Sugar is a constituent of soda.
words.ex_cn: 糖是苏打水的一种成分。
words.en: A constituent is a part of a whole. In politics, a constituent is a person who is represented by an elected official.

words.ex: The constitution protects the rights of all citizens.
words.ex_cn: 宪法保护所有公民的权利。
words.en: The constitution of a country or organization is the system of laws which formally states people's rights and duties.

words.tr: n. 迷信；迷信观念（或思想）；
words.ex: He avoids walking under ladders because of superstition.
words.ex_cn: 他因为迷信而不愿从梯子下走过。
words.en: A superstition is a belief or practice resulting from ignorance, fear of the unknown, trust in magic or chance, or a false conception of causation.

words.tr: adj. 迷信的；有迷信观念的
words.ex: He is superstitious about walking under ladders.
words.ex_cn: 他迷信地认为走过梯子下面会带来厄运。
words.en: Having or showing a belief in superstitions.

chapters.name: 词根 450. stow = place 放置

words.ex: The king will bestow a medal on the hero.
words.ex_cn: 国王将把奖章授予这位英雄。
words.en: To bestow something on someone means to give or present it to them.

chapters.name: 词根 451. straight = stretch 伸展

words.tr: v. （使）变直；（使）变平；（使）变整齐；
words.ex: He straightened the crooked picture on the wall.
words.ex_cn: 他把墙上歪斜的画扶直了。
words.en: To make something straight or to put something in order.

words.ex: The instructions were straightforward and easy to follow.
words.ex_cn: 这些说明很简单，容易遵循。
words.en: If you describe something as straightforward, you approve of it because it is easy to do or understand.

words.ex: He answered the question straightforwardly.
words.ex_cn: 他直接回答了问题。
words.en: In a straightforward manner; directly and without evasion.

chapters.name: 词根 452. strain, straint = tighten 拉紧

words.ex: The law constrains companies from polluting rivers.
words.ex_cn: 法律约束公司不得污染河流。
words.en: To constrain someone or something means to limit their development or force them to behave in a particular way.

words.ex: The budget is a constraint on our project.
words.ex_cn: 预算是我们项目的限制。
words.en: A constraint is something that limits or controls what you can do.

words.ex: He tries to restrain his anger.
words.ex_cn: 他努力克制自己的愤怒。
words.en: If you restrain someone, you stop them from doing what they intended or wanted to do, usually by using your physical strength.

words.ex: He showed restraint when he stayed calm during the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他在争论中保持冷静，表现出了克制。
words.en: Restraint is a measure or condition that keeps someone or something under control or within limits.

chapters.name: 词根 453. strophe = tum 转

words.ex: The earthquake was a catastrophe.
words.ex_cn: 这场地震是一场灾难。
words.en: An event causing great and often sudden damage or suffering; a disaster.

chapters.name: 词根 454. struct = build 建造

words.tr: n. 毁灭；引起毁灭的根源；
words.ex: The storm caused the destruction of the village.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴摧毁了村庄。
words.en: The act of destroying something, or the state of being destroyed.

words.ex: The storm was destructive and broke many houses.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴具有破坏性，摧毁了许多房屋。
words.en: Causing great and irreparable harm or damage.

words.ex: The construction of the new bridge took two years.
words.ex_cn: 新桥的建筑花了两年时间。
words.en: The process or method of building or making something, especially buildings, bridges, etc.

words.ex: The instructor explained the math problem clearly.
words.ex_cn: 教员清楚地讲解了这道数学题。
words.en: An instructor is someone who teaches a skill or subject, especially in a college or university, or in a specialized field such as driving or skiing.

words.ex: The teacher gave clear instruction on how to solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 老师给出了如何解决这个问题的明确教授。
words.en: Detailed information telling how something should be done, operated, or assembled.

words.tr: adj. 有帮助的；乐器的；仪器的；
words.ex: Her advice was instrumental in helping me pass the exam.
words.ex_cn: 她的建议对帮助我通过考试很有帮助。
words.en: If someone or something is instrumental in a process, plan, or system, they are one of the most important influences in causing it to happen.

chapters.name: 词根 455. suad = urge 力劝

words.ex: His persuasion helped me change my mind.
words.ex_cn: 他的说服让我改变了主意。
words.en: Persuasion is the act of persuading someone to do something or to believe that something is true.

words.ex: He tried to persuade her to stay.
words.ex_cn: 他试图说服她留下。
words.en: If you persuade someone to do something, you cause them to do it by giving them good reasons for doing it.

chapters.name: 词根 456. sue = follow 跟随

words.tr: v. 接着发生；因而产生
words.ex: The storm ended, and peace ensued.
words.ex_cn: 风暴结束后，和平随之而来。
words.en: If something ensues, it happens immediately after another event, usually as a result of it.

chapters.name: 词根 457. sult = leap 跳

words.ex: The police investigated the assault on the old man.
words.ex_cn: 警方调查了对那位老人的攻击。
words.en: An assault is a physical attack on someone, or a military attack on a place.

words.tr:
adj. 作为结果的；合成的
n. 结果；产物
words.ex: The resultant force moved the box forward.
words.ex_cn: 合力把箱子向前推了。
words.en: A resultant thing or situation is the one that follows or is caused by a particular event or action.

chapters.name: 词根 458. sum, sumpt = take 拿，取

words.ex: His assumption was that the train would be on time.
words.ex_cn: 他的假设是火车会准时。
words.en: An assumption is something that you assume to be the case, even without proof.

words.ex: The consumer buys food at the store.
words.ex_cn: 消费者在商店购买食物。
words.en: A consumer is a person who buys goods or uses services.

words.ex: The consumption of water has increased this year.
words.ex_cn: 今年水的消耗量增加了。
words.en: Consumption is the act of buying and using products.

words.ex: I presume he will arrive tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我假设他明天会到。
words.en: If you presume that something is the case, you think that it is the case, although you are not certain.

words.tr: n. 假定；推定；冒昧；放肆
words.ex: His presumption that he would win surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他以为自己会赢的这种假设让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: A presumption is something that is thought to be true because it is likely, although there is no proof.

words.ex: He is presumably at home now.
words.ex_cn: 推测起来，他现在在家。
words.en: If you say that something is presumably the case, you mean that you think it is very likely to be the case, although you are not certain.

words.ex: After a short break, he resumed his work.
words.ex_cn: 短暂休息后，他继续工作。
words.en: If you resume an activity or if it resumes, it begins again or continues after an interruption.

chapters.name: 词根 459. summ = add up 总共

words.ex: He gave a summary of the story at the end.
words.ex_cn: 他在结尾对故事做了总结。
words.en: A summary is a brief statement or account of the main points of something.

words.ex: Can you summarize the story in one sentence?
words.ex_cn: 你能用一句话总结这个故事吗？
words.en: If you summarize something, you give a brief description of its main points.

words.ex: The climbers reached the summit of the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 登山者到达了山顶。
words.en: The highest point of a hill or mountain; a meeting between heads of government.

chapters.name: 词根 460. super = up 在上面

words.ex: His superiority in math helped him win the contest.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学上的优越让他赢得了比赛。
words.en: If one side in a war or conflict has superiority, it has an advantage over its enemy, for example because it has more soldiers or better equipment.

words.ex: This phone is superior to the old one.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机比旧的更好。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as superior, you mean that they are better than other people or things.

chapters.name: 词根 461. sur = sure 肯定

words.ex: He gave me his assurance that the work would be done on time.
words.ex_cn: 他向我保证工作会按时完成。
words.en: If you give someone an assurance that something is true or will happen, you say that it is definitely true or will definitely happen, in order to make them feel less worried.

words.ex: Mom reassured me that everything would be fine.
words.ex_cn: 妈妈让我安心，一切都会好起来的。
words.en: If you reassure someone, you comfort them and stop them from worrying.

words.ex: His smile gave me reassurance.
words.ex_cn: 他的微笑让我安心。
words.en: If someone needs reassurance, they are very worried and need someone to help them stop worrying by saying kind or helpful things.

chapters.name: 词根 462. sur = excess 超过

words.tr: adj. 荒唐的；荒唐可笑的；
words.ex: It's absurd to wear a coat in summer.
words.ex_cn: 夏天穿外套是荒唐的。
words.en: If you say that something is absurd, you are criticizing it because you think that it is ridiculous or that it does not make sense.

chapters.name: 词根 463. syst = combine 联合

words.ex: He follows a systematic approach to solve math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他用一种系统的方法来解决数学问题。
words.en: A systematic approach or method is one that is done according to a fixed plan, in a thorough and efficient way.

words.tr: adv. 有系统地；有组织地；
words.ex: He systematically organized his books by subject.
words.ex_cn: 他有系统地按科目整理了他的书。
words.en: in a thorough, methodical, and organized manner

chapters.name: 词根 464. tabul = plank 平板

words.ex: The data was tabulated for easier analysis.
words.ex_cn: 数据被制成表格以便于分析。
words.en: To tabulate something means to arrange figures, facts, or information in a table or list so that it can be easily understood or compared.

words.ex: He made a tabulation of the survey results.
words.ex_cn: 他对调查结果进行了列表整理。
words.en: The act of arranging data in a table or tabular form.

chapters.name: 词根 465. tach = connect 连接

words.tr: n. 依恋；附件；附加装置；
words.ex: The child showed strong attachment to his teddy bear.
words.ex_cn: 孩子对他的泰迪熊产生了强烈的依恋。
words.en: An attachment is a file that is sent along with an email message.

words.ex: He tried to detach himself from the group.
words.ex_cn: 他试图脱离这个群体。
words.en: If you detach one thing from another that it is fixed to, you remove it. If one thing detaches from another, it becomes separated from it.

words.tr: n. 分离；拆开；支队；超然；分遣队
words.ex: The detachment of the two teams caused confusion.
words.ex_cn: 两个团队的分离造成了混乱。
words.en: If you refer to someone's detachment, you mean that they do not become involved in other people's problems or emotions, or that they do not show their own feelings.

chapters.name: 词根 466. tact, tang, tamin = touch 接触

words.tr:
n. 接触；联系；
v. 接触；联系；
words.ex: The two balls made contact when they collided.
words.ex_cn: 两个球在碰撞时发生了接触。
words.en: Contact refers to the act of communicating with someone, especially regularly, or the state of touching something.

words.ex: The river is contaminated by factory waste.
words.ex_cn: 这条河被工厂废料污染了。
words.en: To contaminate something means to make it impure or polluted by contact or mixture with something unclean or harmful.

words.ex: The river suffered from contamination after the factory dumped waste.
words.ex_cn: 工厂倾倒废物后，这条河受到了污染。
words.en: The process of making something dirty or polluted, or the state of being dirty or polluted.

words.ex: The water has a dangerous contaminant.
words.ex_cn: 这种水含有危险的污染物。
words.en: A contaminant is something that makes a place or a substance (such as water, air, or food) no longer suitable for use, often by adding harmful substances to it.

words.ex: The vase remained intact after the fall.
words.ex_cn: 花瓶从高处摔下后依然完整无缺。
words.en: Something that is intact is complete and has not been damaged or changed.

words.ex: He answered the question with tact.
words.ex_cn: 他机智地回答了这个问题。
words.en: If you describe what someone says or does as tact, you mean that it is polite, considerate, and shows an understanding of other people's feelings.

words.tr: adj. 机智的；圆滑的；得体的
words.ex: He was tactful when he said no to her request.
words.ex_cn: 当他拒绝她的请求时，他很得体。
words.en: If you describe someone as tactful, you approve of them because they are careful not to say or do anything that would offend or upset other people.

words.tr: adj. 不机智的；不机敏的；不老练的；不圆滑的；不乖巧的
words.ex: He was tactless when he criticized her in front of everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他在众人面前批评她，显得很不妥当。
words.en: If you describe someone as tactless, you think what they say or do is likely to offend other people.

words.ex: The coach changed his tactics to win the game.
words.ex_cn: 教练改变了策略以赢得比赛。
words.en: Tactics are the methods that you choose to use in order to achieve what you want in a particular situation.

words.tr: adj. 战术上的；有谋略的；手段高明的
words.ex: He made a tactical move to win the game.
words.ex_cn: 他做了一个战术性的举动来赢得比赛。
words.en: relating to or constituting actions carefully planned to gain a specific military end.

words.tr: adj. 可触摸的；实际的；有形的；确凿的；
words.ex: The statue is tangible and can be touched.
words.ex_cn: 这座雕像可以触摸，是实实在在的。
words.en: Something that is tangible is clear enough or definite enough to be easily seen, felt, or noticed.

chapters.name: 词根 467. tail = cut 切割

words.ex: He noticed every detail of the painting.
words.ex_cn: 他注意到了这幅画的每一个细节。
words.en: A detail is a small individual feature or element of something.

words.ex: He works in retail at a small store.
words.ex_cn: 他在一家小店从事零售工作。
words.en: The sale of goods to the public in relatively small quantities for use or consumption rather than for resale.

chapters.name: 词根 468. tain, ten, tin = hold 握，拿

words.tr: adj. 欧洲大陆的；大陆的；
words.ex: He prefers continental breakfast with bread and coffee.
words.ex_cn: 他更喜欢欧洲大陆式的早餐，有面包和咖啡。
words.en: Continental is used to describe something that relates to or is characteristic of a continent, especially the mainland of Europe as distinct from the British Isles.

words.ex: The continuity of the story made it easy to follow.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事的连续性让它容易理解。
words.en: Continuity is the fact that something continues to happen or exist, with no great changes or interruptions.

words.ex: The rain was continuous all day.
words.ex_cn: 雨一整天都在下个不停。
words.en: Something that is continuous happens or exists without stopping or being interrupted.

words.ex: The police will detain the suspect for questioning.
words.ex_cn: 警察将扣留嫌疑人进行审问。
words.en: If someone is detained, they are officially held in a place, especially a prison, and are not allowed to leave.

words.ex: Watching movies is a popular entertainment.
words.ex_cn: 看电影是一种流行的休闲娱乐。
words.en: Entertainment refers to performances or activities that are intended to amuse or interest an audience.

words.ex: His answer was pertinent to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答与问题相关。
words.en: Something that is pertinent is relevant to a particular subject.

words.ex: The company improved data retention after upgrading its system.
words.ex_cn: 公司在升级系统后提高了数据保留能力。
words.en: The action of retaining something; the continued possession, use, or control of something.

words.tr: adj. 记性好的；有保持力的
words.ex: She has a very retentive memory.
words.ex_cn: 她有非常好的记忆力。
words.en: If you have a retentive memory, you are able to remember things easily.

words.ex: The farmer works hard to sustain his crops.
words.ex_cn: 这位农民努力维持他的庄稼。
words.en: To sustain something means to continue it or maintain it for a period of time.

chapters.name: 词根 469. tard = slow 慢

words.ex: The rain will retard the construction of the road.
words.ex_cn: 雨水会延迟道路的建设。
words.en: To retard something means to delay it or make it happen more slowly than it would otherwise.

chapters.name: 词根 470. tect = cover 掩盖

words.ex: The detective solved the mystery with clues.
words.ex_cn: 侦探用线索破解了谜案。
words.en: A detective is someone whose job is to discover what has happened in a crime or other situation and to find the people involved.

words.ex: The detection of smoke triggered the alarm.
words.ex_cn: 烟雾的探测触发了警报。
words.en: The act of detecting something, especially something that is not easy to see, hear, etc.

words.tr: n. 探测器；检测器；发现者；
words.ex: The detector found a hidden metal object.
words.ex_cn: 探测器发现了一个隐藏的金属物体。
words.en: A detector is a device that is used to discover the presence of something, such as smoke, metal, or radiation.

chapters.name: 词根 471. tele = far 远，引申为“电”

words.ex: Telecommunications connect people across the world.
words.ex_cn: 电信连接了全世界的人们。
words.en: Telecommunications is the technology of sending signals and messages over long distances using electronic means, such as radio, telephone, television, and the internet.

words.tr:
n. 电传
v. 发电传
words.ex: He sent a telex to confirm the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他发了一份电传以确认会议。
words.en: A telex is a communication system consisting of teletypewriters connected to a telephonic network to send and receive signals.

chapters.name: 词根 472. temper, tempo = time 时间或由时间引起的现象

words.ex: His calm temperament helps him stay peaceful in stress.
words.ex_cn: 他平静的性情让他在压力下保持平和。
words.en: Your temperament is your basic nature, especially as it is shown in the way that you react to situations or to other people.

words.ex: The drummer changed the tempo of the song.
words.ex_cn: 鼓手改变了这首歌的拍子。
words.en: The speed at which a piece of music is played or the rate or speed of motion or activity.

chapters.name: 词根 473. templ = space for observing auguries 观看占卜仪式的空地

words.tr: v. 考虑；深思；凝视；思考…的可能性
words.ex: He contemplates quitting his job.
words.ex_cn: 他正在考虑辞去工作。
words.en: If you contemplate an action, you think about whether to do it or not.

chapters.name: 词根 474. tempt = try 尝试

words.ex: He looked at the lie with contempt.
words.ex_cn: 他轻蔑地看着这个谎言。
words.en: If you have contempt for someone or something, you have no respect for them or think that they are unimportant.

chapters.name: 词根 475. tend, tens, tent = stretch 伸

words.ex: His attendance at the meeting was mandatory.
words.ex_cn: 他必须出席这次会议。
words.en: The act of being present at a place or event.

words.tr:
n. 服务人员
adj. 随之而来的
words.ex: The attendant helped me find my seat.
words.ex_cn: 服务员帮我找到了座位。
words.en: An attendant is someone whose job is to serve or help people in a public place.

words.ex: He contends that education is the key to success.
words.ex_cn: 他主张教育是成功的关键。
words.en: If you contend with someone or contend with something, you have to deal with a difficult situation or problem. If you contend that something is true, you state or argue that it is true.

words.ex: There was a contention between the two students about the answer.
words.ex_cn: 两个学生对答案发生了争论。
words.en: A contention is a strong disagreement or argument about something. It can also refer to a point or statement that someone argues is true.

words.tr: n. 扩展；延长期；延伸；电话分机；
words.ex: The company added an extension to its office building.
words.ex_cn: 公司为办公楼加了一个扩建部分。
words.en: An extension is a part that is added to something to make it longer or larger, or the act of adding this part.

words.tr: adj. 广大的；广阔的；广泛的；大量的；
words.ex: He has extensive knowledge of history.
words.ex_cn: 他拥有广博的历史知识。
words.en: Something that is extensive covers a wide area or includes a lot of things.

words.ex: The storm will intensify tonight.
words.ex_cn: 风暴今晚会加强。
words.en: To make or become more intense or intensive.

words.ex: He took an intensive English course last summer.
words.ex_cn: 去年夏天，他参加了一个密集的英语课程。
words.en: Intensive is used to describe something that involves a lot of effort, energy, or attention in a short period of time.

words.tr:
n. 意图；目的；
adj. 专注的；
words.ex: His intent was to help, not to hurt.
words.ex_cn: 他的意图是帮助，而不是伤害。
words.en: If you are intent on doing something, you are determined to get it done. If you have an intent to do something, you have a plan or purpose in mind.

words.ex: The rope has high tensile strength.
words.ex_cn: 这根绳子有很高的抗拉强度。
words.en: relating to tension; capable of being stretched or drawn out

words.tr: n. 紧张；紧张局势；紧张关系；
words.ex: There was tension between the two friends after the argument.
words.ex_cn: 两人争吵后，彼此之间出现了紧张。
words.en: Tension is a feeling of worry and anxiety which makes it difficult for you to relax. It can also refer to the state of being stretched tight or the degree of tightness of a stretched string, wire, etc.

chapters.name: 词根 476. tent = try 尝试

words.tr: adj. 暂定的；不确定的；试验性的；
words.ex: We made a tentative plan to meet next week.
words.ex_cn: 我们制定了一个下周见面的暂定计划。
words.en: If you make a tentative suggestion or plan, you make it without being sure that it is right or acceptable.

chapters.name: 词根 477. termin = limit 界限，限定

words.ex: The bus stops at the terminal at 9 PM.
words.ex_cn: 公交车晚上9点到达终点站。
words.en: A terminal is a place where vehicles, passengers, or goods begin or end a journey. It can also refer to a computer device at which a user enters data or commands.

words.ex: The train stops at the terminus.
words.ex_cn: 火车在终点站停下。
words.en: A terminus is the end of a transportation line or the station at the end of a railway or bus route.

words.ex: The teacher will terminate the class at 5 p.m.
words.ex_cn: 老师将在下午5点结束课程。
words.en: To terminate something means to bring it to an end or to stop it from continuing.

words.ex: The termination of the contract surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 合同的终止让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: The act of ending something or the end of something.

words.ex: The doctor used medical terminology to explain the illness.
words.ex_cn: 医生使用医学术语来解释这种疾病。
words.en: The set of terms and expressions used in a particular subject, field, or profession.

words.tr: adj. 术语的；术语学的；专门名词的
words.ex: The terminological error confused the students.
words.ex_cn: 这个术语错误让学生们感到困惑。
words.en: Relating to the study or use of terms and their definitions.

chapters.name: 词根 478. terr = land 土地

words.ex: The house has a small terrace with chairs.
words.ex_cn: 这所房子有一个带椅子的小平台。
words.en: A terrace is a flat area of stone or grass next to a building where people can sit.

words.ex: The hikers struggled across the rough terrain.
words.ex_cn: 徒步者艰难地穿越了崎岖的地形。
words.en: Terrain is used to refer to an area of land or a type of land when you are considering its physical features.

chapters.name: 词根 479. terr = frighten 害怕

words.ex: The concert was terrific!
words.ex_cn: 这场音乐会太棒了！
words.en: If you describe something or someone as terrific, you are very pleased with them or very impressed by them.

words.tr: adv. 极端地；可怕地；非常地
words.ex: She did terrifically on the math test.
words.ex_cn: 她在数学考试中表现得非常好。
words.en: Extremely or very much.

words.ex: The loud thunder terrified the child.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的雷声吓坏了那个孩子。
words.en: If something terrifies you, it makes you feel extremely frightened.

words.ex: The police caught the terrorist near the station.
words.ex_cn: 警察在车站附近抓住了这名恐怖分子。
words.en: A terrorist is a person who uses violent and intimidating methods in the pursuit of political aims.

words.tr: n. 恐怖主义；恐怖行动
words.ex: The country is fighting terrorism with strong laws.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家通过严格的法律打击恐怖主义。
words.en: Terrorism is the use of violence and intimidation in the pursuit of political aims.

chapters.name: 词根 480. test = witness 证据

words.ex: He testified that he saw the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他证明自己看到了那起事故。
words.en: To testify means to make a statement based on personal knowledge or belief, especially in a court of law, or to serve as evidence or proof of something's existence or truth.

words.ex: His testimony proved the suspect was innocent.
words.ex_cn: 他的证词证明了嫌疑人是无辜的。
words.en: A formal written or spoken statement, especially one given in a court of law.

chapters.name: 词根 481. text = weave 编织

words.ex: The word means different things in different context.
words.ex_cn: 这个词在不同的上下文中意思不同。
words.en: The context of an idea or event is the general situation that relates to it, and which helps it to be understood.

words.tr: adj. 上下文的；前后关系的；
words.ex: The meaning of the word depends on its contextual use.
words.ex_cn: 这个词的含义取决于它的上下文用法。
words.en: relating to or depending on the context of something

words.ex: He used a pretext to leave the meeting early.
words.ex_cn: 他找了个借口提前离开了会议。
words.en: A pretext is a false reason that you give for doing something, usually something bad, in order to hide the real reason.

words.ex: The texture of the bread is soft and fluffy.
words.ex_cn: 这种面包的质地柔软蓬松。
words.en: The feel, appearance, or consistency of a surface or a substance.

chapters.name: 词根 482. theo = god 神

words.tr: adj. 充满热情的；热心的；
words.ex: He is enthusiastic about playing basketball.
words.ex_cn: 他对打篮球充满热情。
words.en: If you are enthusiastic about something, you show how much you like or enjoy it by the way that you behave and talk.

words.ex: He showed great enthusiasm for learning English.
words.ex_cn: 他对学习英语表现出极大的热情。
words.en: Enthusiasm is a strong feeling of excitement and interest in something and a desire to become involved in it.

chapters.name: 词根 483. therm = heat 热

words.ex: The thermal blanket keeps you warm.
words.ex_cn: 这个保暖毯让你暖和。
words.en: relating to heat or temperature

words.ex: He checked the thermometer to see the temperature.
words.ex_cn: 他看了温度计来查看温度。
words.en: A thermometer is an instrument for measuring and indicating temperature.

chapters.name: 词根 484. thesis = place 放置

words.ex: He made a hypothesis that plants grow faster in light.
words.ex_cn: 他提出一个假设，认为植物在光照下长得更快。
words.en: A hypothesis is an idea which is suggested as a possible explanation for a particular situation or condition, but which has not yet been proved to be correct.

words.ex: The synthesis of ideas helped solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 这些想法的综合帮助解决了问题。
words.en: The act of combining different ideas, influences, or objects into a new and coherent whole.

words.ex: The shirt is made of synthetic fabric.
words.ex_cn: 这件衬衫是合成纤维制成的。
words.en: Synthetic products are made from chemicals or artificial substances rather than from natural ones.

words.ex: His thesis is that exercise improves memory.
words.ex_cn: 他的论点是锻炼能改善记忆力。
words.en: A thesis is a long piece of writing based on your own ideas and research that you do as part of a university degree, especially a higher degree such as a PhD.

chapters.name: 词根 485. tim = fear 害怕

words.ex: The bully tried to intimidate the new student.
words.ex_cn: 那个霸凌者试图恐吓新生。
words.en: If you intimidate someone, you deliberately make them frightened enough to do what you want them to do.

words.ex: The timid boy whispered his answer.
words.ex_cn: 这个害羞的男孩小声说出了他的答案。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior or actions as timid, you are criticizing them for being too cautious or slow to act, because they are nervous about the possible consequences of their actions.

words.ex: His timidity made him afraid to speak in class.
words.ex_cn: 他的胆怯让他不敢在课堂上发言。
words.en: The quality or state of being timid; lack of courage or self-confidence.

chapters.name: 词根 486. title = caption 题字

words.tr: v. 授权；命名；给...权利（或资格）
words.ex: This book entitles you to a free gift.
words.ex_cn: 这本书使你有资格获得一份免费礼物。
words.en: If you are entitled to something, you have the right to have it or do it.

chapters.name: 词根 487. toler = endure 容忍

words.ex: My teacher is tolerant of different opinions.
words.ex_cn: 我的老师对不同的观点很宽容。
words.en: If you describe someone as tolerant, you approve of the fact that they allow other people to say and do as they like, even if they do not agree with or like it.

words.ex: His tolerance for different opinions is impressive.
words.ex_cn: 他对不同观点的宽容令人印象深刻。
words.en: The ability or willingness to tolerate the existence of opinions or behaviour that one dislikes or disagrees with.

chapters.name: 词根 488. ton = voice 声音

words.ex: His intonation made the sentence sound friendly.
words.ex_cn: 他的语调让这句话听起来很友好。
words.en: Intonation is the way the voice rises and falls in speech, especially the pitch pattern in a sentence.

chapters.name: 词根 489. tort = twist 扭

words.ex: The mirror distorts my face.
words.ex_cn: 这面镜子扭曲了我的脸。
words.en: If you distort a statement, fact, or idea, you report or represent it in an untrue way.

words.tr: n. 扭曲；歪曲；失真；畸变；
words.ex: The photo showed distortion in the lines.
words.ex_cn: 这张照片中的线条出现了扭曲。
words.en: A distortion is a change, twist, or exaggeration that makes something appear different from the way it really is.

words.tr:
v. 反驳；回嘴
n. 反驳；顶嘴
words.ex: He gave a quick retort when she criticized him.
words.ex_cn: 当她批评他时，他迅速回了一句。
words.en: If you retort, you reply angrily to someone.

words.ex: He called her names, and she gave him retortion.
words.ex_cn: 他骂她，她也回骂了他。
words.en: Retortion refers to the act of returning a wrong or injury in kind; retaliation.

words.tr:
n. 痛苦；折磨；令人痛苦的东西
v. 折磨；使痛苦；烦扰；纠缠；戏弄
words.ex: The loss of his dog was a deep torment.
words.ex_cn: 失去他的狗是一种深深的痛苦。
words.en: Torment refers to severe physical or mental suffering, or to cause someone to experience such suffering.

words.tr:
n. 酷刑；拷打
v. 拷打；折磨
words.ex: The prisoner suffered from torture during the war.
words.ex_cn: 这名囚犯在战争期间遭受了酷刑。
words.en: Torture is the act of deliberately inflicting severe physical or psychological pain on someone, typically to extract information or a confession, or as a punishment.

chapters.name: 词根 490. torn = turn 转

words.tr: n. 律师；辩护律师；代理人
words.ex: The attorney helped the man with his case.
words.ex_cn: 律师帮助那个人处理了他的案件。
words.en: An attorney is a lawyer who is qualified to represent a client in court.

chapters.name: 词根 491. tox = poison 毒

words.ex: The water is toxic to fish.
words.ex_cn: 这种水对鱼是有毒的。
words.en: If a substance is toxic, it is poisonous.

chapters.name: 词根 492. tract = draw 拉，抽

words.tr:
adj. 抽象的；非具体的；
n. 摘要；概要；抽象派艺术作品；
words.ex: The painting shows an abstract shape.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画展示了一个抽象的形状。
words.en: An abstract idea or way of thinking is based on general ideas rather than on real things and events.

words.tr: n. 出神；心不在焉；抽象
words.ex: He sat by the window in abstraction, staring at the clouds.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在窗边出神，凝视着云朵。
words.en: An abstraction is a general idea rather than one that is based on a specific real thing or event.

words.tr:
n. 合同；契约；
v. 收缩；
words.ex: They signed a contract to buy the house.
words.ex_cn: 他们签署了一份购买房子的合同。
words.en: A contract is a legal agreement between two or more parties. It can also mean to become smaller or tighter, or to catch a disease.

words.ex: The loud music distract me from my homework.
words.ex_cn: 嘈杂的音乐让我无法专心做作业。
words.en: If something distracts you or your attention, it makes you stop concentrating on what you are doing.

words.ex: The loud music was a distraction while I tried to study.
words.ex_cn: 当我试图学习时，大声的音乐让我分心。
words.en: Something that makes it difficult for you to concentrate on what you are doing.

words.tr:
v. 提取；
n. 摘录；提取物；
words.ex: They extract oil from plants.
words.ex_cn: 他们从植物中提取油。
words.en: To remove or take out something, especially by effort or force.

words.ex: The extraction of coal harms the environment.
words.ex_cn: 煤炭的开采对环境有害。
words.en: The process of removing or obtaining something from something else.

chapters.name: 词根 493. treat = handle 处理

words.ex: He entreats his friend to help him.
words.ex_cn: 他恳求朋友帮助他。
words.en: To ask someone earnestly or anxiously to do something.

words.ex: She made an earnest entreaty for forgiveness.
words.ex_cn: 她真诚地恳求原谅。
words.en: An entreaty is a serious and often emotional request for something, especially for help or mercy.

chapters.name: 词根 494. trench = cut 切割

words.ex: The workers dug a trench to lay the pipe.
words.ex_cn: 工人们挖了一条沟来铺设管道。
words.en: A trench is a long, narrow ditch. In warfare, trenches are dug by troops to provide shelter from enemy fire.

chapters.name: 词根 495. tribut = give 给予

words.tr:
v. 把…归因于；由…引起；
n. 品质；属性；特征；属性；
words.ex: He attributes his success to hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他把他的成功归因于努力工作。
words.en: If you attribute something to an event or situation, you think that it was caused by that event or situation.

words.ex: He gave attribution to the original writer.
words.ex_cn: 他把功劳归于原作者。
words.en: The action of regarding something as being caused by a person or thing.

chapters.name: 词根 496. tric = trifle 琐碎

words.ex: The intricacy of the clock made it very special.
words.ex_cn: 这座钟的复杂精细让它非常特别。
words.en: The quality of being intricate; complexity.

words.ex: The lock has an intricate design.
words.ex_cn: 这个锁有复杂的结构。
words.en: You use intricate to describe something that has many small parts or details.

words.tr:
v. 密谋；激起…的兴趣
n. 阴谋诡计；密谋策划
words.ex: They intrigue to take over the company.
words.ex_cn: 他们密谋接管这家公司。
words.en: If something intrigues you, it interests you a lot because it seems strange or mysterious.

chapters.name: 词根 497. trieve = find 得到

words.ex: He went back to retrieve his keys.
words.ex_cn: 他回去取回他的钥匙。
words.en: To retrieve something means to get it back from somewhere, especially after it has been lost or taken away.

chapters.name: 词根 498. trop = turn 转

words.tr:
n. 回归线；热带
adj. 热带的
words.ex: The Tropic of Cancer is north of the equator.
words.ex_cn: 北回归线在赤道以北。
words.en: The tropics are the region of the Earth surrounding the Equator. They are delimited in latitude by the Tropic of Cancer in the Northern Hemisphere at 23°26′10.0″ (or 23.4361°) N and the Tropic of Capricorn in the Southern Hemisphere at 23°26′10.0″ (or 23.4361°) S; these latitudes correspond to the axial tilt of the Earth.

words.ex: He lives in a tropical island near the equator.
words.ex_cn: 他住在赤道附近的一个热带岛屿上。
words.en: relating to or situated in or characteristic of the tropics (the region on either side of the equator)

chapters.name: 词根 499. tuit = look 看

words.ex: I trusted my intuition and chose the right answer.
words.ex_cn: 我相信自己的直觉，选了正确的答案。
words.en: Intuition is the ability to understand or know something immediately, without the need for conscious reasoning.

words.ex: The app has an intuitive design.
words.ex_cn: 这个应用程序具有直观的设计。
words.en: An intuitive idea or feeling is based on an instinctive emotional response rather than on conscious thought.

chapters.name: 词根 500. turb = stir 搅动

words.ex: The noise from the construction caused a disturbance.
words.ex_cn: 建筑工地的噪音造成了干扰。
words.en: A disturbance is an event or situation in which people behave in a noisy or violent way, or something that interrupts what you are doing.

words.tr: adj. 狂暴的；骚动的；动荡的；汹涌的
words.ex: The turbulent sea made the boat shake.
words.ex_cn: 汹涌的海让船摇晃。
words.en: A turbulent situation, time, or relationship is one in which there is a lot of change, confusion, and often conflict.

words.ex: The political turbulence caused many people to leave the country.
words.ex_cn: 政治骚乱导致许多人离开了这个国家。
words.en: A state of conflict or confusion; irregular atmospheric motion especially when characterized by up-and-down currents.

chapters.name: 词根 501. tut, tuit = protect 保护

words.ex: The tuition for this course is $500.
words.ex_cn: 这门课程的学费是500美元。
words.en: Tuition is the fee charged for instruction, especially at a college, university, or private school.

chapters.name: 词根 502. tyrant = tyrannus 暴君

words.ex: The people rose up against the tyranny of the king.
words.ex_cn: 人民反抗了国王的暴虐。
words.en: Tyranny is cruel and unfair treatment by someone with power over other people, or a government in which a single ruler has absolute power.

words.ex: The tyrant ruled the country with fear.
words.ex_cn: 暴君用恐惧统治国家。
words.en: A tyrant is a ruler who has complete power in a country and uses it in a cruel and unfair way.

words.tr: adj. 暴虐的；压制的；残暴的
words.ex: The tyrannical king punished people for small mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 这个暴虐的国王因为小错误惩罚人民。
words.en: Using power in a cruel and unfair way over people in a country or group.

chapters.name: 词根 503. ultim = last 最后的

words.tr: adj. 最终的；最后的；极端的；
words.ex: This is the ultimate solution to the problem.
words.ex_cn: 这是这个问题的最终解决方案。
words.en: You use ultimate to describe the final result or aim of a long series of events.

chapters.name: 词根 504. un, uni = one 单一，一个

words.ex: The family had a reunion last Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 这家人上个星期天举行了团聚。
words.en: A reunion is a gathering of people who have been separated, especially members of a family or old friends, coming together again.

words.tr: v. （使）统一；（使）联合；（使）成一体；
words.ex: The two teams decided to unify their efforts.
words.ex_cn: 这两个团队决定统一他们的努力。
words.en: To unify means to make or become united, uniform, or whole.

words.ex: The unification of the two countries brought peace.
words.ex_cn: 两个国家的统一带来了和平。
words.en: The process of making or becoming a single unit.

words.ex: This painting is unique because no other like it exists.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画是独特的，因为没有其他类似的。
words.en: Something that is unique is the only one of its kind.

words.ex: This rule is universally accepted.
words.ex_cn: 这条规则被普遍接受。
words.en: In a way that is done or shared by all people or things in the world or in a particular group.

words.tr: v. 使一般化；使普遍化
words.ex: The government aims to universalize healthcare.
words.ex_cn: 政府旨在使医疗保健普遍化。
words.en: To make something universal or applicable to all cases.

chapters.name: 词根 505. und = wave 波浪

words.ex: There is an abundance of food at the party.
words.ex_cn: 聚会上食物非常丰富。
words.en: A very large quantity of something.

words.ex: The forest has abundant water and trees.
words.ex_cn: 这片森林水源和树木都很丰富。
words.en: If something is abundant, there is a lot of it or it is very common.

words.ex: The extra chair is redundant because we have enough seats.
words.ex_cn: 这把额外的椅子是多余的，因为我们已经有足够的座位了。
words.en: If you are made redundant, your employer tells you to leave because your job is no longer necessary or because there is no more work for you.

chapters.name: 词根 506. ut = use 用

words.ex: He picked up a spoon, a common utensil.
words.ex_cn: 他拿起了一把勺子，一种常见的餐具。
words.en: An utensil is a tool that you use in your home, especially in the kitchen, for example, a knife, fork, or spoon.

words.ex: The utilization of solar energy is increasing.
words.ex_cn: 太阳能的利用正在增加。
words.en: Utilization is the act of using something effectively.

chapters.name: 词根 507. vac = empty 空的

words.ex: The police told everyone to evacuate the building.
words.ex_cn: 警察让所有人撤离大楼。
words.en: To evacuate means to remove people from a place of danger to a safer place.

words.ex: The city ordered an evacuation because of the fire.
words.ex_cn: 由于火灾，城市下令疏散。
words.en: The process of moving people from a dangerous place to somewhere safe.

chapters.name: 词根 508. vad, vag = go 走

words.ex: He tried to evade the police by driving fast.
words.ex_cn: 他试图通过高速驾驶来逃避警察。
words.en: If you evade something, you find a way of not doing something that you really ought to do.

words.ex: He tried evasion to avoid paying taxes.
words.ex_cn: 他试图逃避缴税。
words.en: The act of avoiding something that you are supposed to do or deal with.

words.ex: He bought an extravagant car that cost too much money.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一辆奢侈的车，价格太贵了。
words.en: Spending much more than is necessary or wise; excessively expensive.

words.ex: He bought a luxury car as an extravagance.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一辆豪华汽车作为奢侈品。
words.en: Extravagance refers to the spending of more money than is reasonable or than you can afford, or the use of more of something than is necessary.

chapters.name: 词根 509. vail, val = strong 强壮

words.ex: He did not avail himself of the opportunity.
words.ex_cn: 他没有利用这个机会。
words.en: If you avail yourself of something, you use it or take advantage of it.

words.tr: adj. 可获得的；有空的；可用的；
words.ex: The books are available in the library.
words.ex_cn: 这些书在图书馆里可以借到。
words.en: If something is available, it is able to be used or obtained.

words.ex: The availability of free Wi-Fi is important for travelers.
words.ex_cn: 免费Wi-Fi的可用性对旅行者很重要。
words.en: The quality of being able to be used or obtained.

words.tr: adj. 普遍的；流行的；盛行的；
words.ex: Smoking is prevalent in that country.
words.ex_cn: 在那个国家，吸烟很普遍。
words.en: If a condition, practice, or belief is prevalent, it is common or widespread.

words.ex: The prevalence of flu increased in winter.
words.ex_cn: 流感在冬季更加流行。
words.en: The fact or condition of being prevalent; commonness.

words.ex: The validity of the test results is important.
words.ex_cn: 测试结果的有效性很重要。
words.en: The quality of being logically or factually sound; soundness or cogency.

words.ex: The ticket is invalid because it expired.
words.ex_cn: 这张票无效，因为它已经过期了。
words.en: If something is invalid, it is not legally or officially acceptable, or it is not based on truth or reason.

words.tr: adj. 有价值的；贵重的；值钱的；
words.ex: This old book is valuable to historians.
words.ex_cn: 这本旧书对历史学家来说很有价值。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as valuable, you mean that they are very useful and helpful.

words.ex: The shopkeeper will evaluate the old watch.
words.ex_cn: 店主将估价这块旧手表。
words.en: If you evaluate something or someone, you consider them in order to make a judgment about them, for example about how good or bad they are.

words.tr: adj. 无价的；非常宝贵的；
words.ex: Her advice was invaluable to me.
words.ex_cn: 她的建议对我而言是无价的。
words.en: If you describe something as invaluable, you mean that it is extremely useful.

chapters.name: 词根 510. vapor = steam 蒸汽

words.ex: The sun makes the puddle evaporate quickly.
words.ex_cn: 太阳使水坑很快蒸发。
words.en: If a liquid evaporates, or if something evaporates it, it changes from a liquid state to a gas, because its temperature has increased.

words.ex: Water evaporation happens when the sun heats the lake.
words.ex_cn: 当太阳加热湖泊时，水就会蒸发。
words.en: Evaporation is the process by which a liquid turns into a gas.

chapters.name: 词根 511. vari = change 变化

words.ex: He is invariably late for meetings.
words.ex_cn: 他总是开会迟到。
words.en: If something invariably happens or is invariably true, it always happens or is always true.

chapters.name: 词根 512. veil = cover 盖上

words.ex: The letter revealed his secret.
words.ex_cn: 这封信揭露了他的秘密。
words.en: To reveal something means to make known something that was previously secret or unknown.

words.tr: n. 揭露；被揭示的真相；
words.ex: The letter was a revelation about his secret life.
words.ex_cn: 这封信揭露了他隐秘的生活。
words.en: A revelation is a surprising and previously unknown fact that has been disclosed to others.

words.ex: She wore a white veil on her wedding day.
words.ex_cn: 她在婚礼那天戴了一条白色的面纱。
words.en: A veil is a piece of thin soft cloth that women sometimes wear over their heads and which can also cover their face.

chapters.name: 词根 513. ven, vent = come 来

words.ex: The advent of smartphones changed how we communicate.
words.ex_cn: 智能手机的到来改变了我们的交流方式。
words.en: The arrival of a notable person, thing, or event.

words.ex: The committee will convene tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 委员会明天将召开会议。
words.en: If someone convenes a meeting or conference, they arrange for it to take place. They can also be said to convene when they meet.

words.ex: It is a convention to shake hands when you meet someone.
words.ex_cn: 见面时握手是一种习俗。
words.en: A convention is a large meeting of an organization or political group, or a way of behaving that is considered to be correct or polite by most people in a society.

words.ex: He wears conventional clothes to work.
words.ex_cn: 他穿传统服装去上班。
words.en: Conventional ideas, methods, or systems are the ones that are generally accepted and used, and that have been used for a long time.

words.ex: The teacher intervened when the students argued.
words.ex_cn: 当学生们争吵时，老师进行了干涉。
words.en: If you intervene in a situation, you become involved in it and try to change it.

words.ex: The teacher made an intervention to help the student.
words.ex_cn: 老师进行了干预以帮助学生。
words.en: Intervention is the act of intervening, especially in a situation to prevent something undesirable from happening.

words.ex: The store made an inventory of all the products.
words.ex_cn: 商店对所有商品做了一份清单。
words.en: An inventory is a detailed list of all the items in a place.

words.ex: Handwashing is a simple prevention of disease.
words.ex_cn: 洗手是预防疾病的一种简单方法。
words.en: The act of stopping something from happening or arising.

words.ex: The company's revenue increased last year.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司的收入去年增加了。
words.en: Revenue is the income that a company, organization, or government receives regularly.

chapters.name: 词根 514. venge = avenge 报复

words.tr:
n. 报复；报仇
v. 报复
words.ex: He wanted revenge for his brother's death.
words.ex_cn: 他想为他兄弟的死报仇。
words.en: Revenge involves hurting or punishing someone who has hurt or harmed you.

words.ex: He wanted vengeance after his brother was hurt.
words.ex_cn: 他哥哥被伤害后，他想要报复。
words.en: Vengeance is the act of doing something harmful or unpleasant to someone because they have done something harmful or unpleasant to you.

chapters.name: 词根 515. vent = wind 风

words.ex: The smoke came out of the vent.
words.ex_cn: 烟从排气口飘了出来。
words.en: A vent is a hole or opening that allows air, gas, or liquid to pass out of or into a confined space.

words.ex: Open the window to ventilate the room.
words.ex_cn: 打开窗户给房间通风。
words.en: To ventilate means to cause fresh air to enter and move around a room, building, etc., or to express your opinions or feelings about something openly.

words.ex: The room has good ventilation through the windows.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间通过窗户有良好的通风。
words.en: The provision of fresh air to a room, building, etc., or the system that does this.

chapters.name: 词根 516. ver = true 真实的

words.ex: The jury gave a guilty verdict.
words.ex_cn: 陪审团作出了有罪裁决。
words.en: A verdict is a decision made after a lot of consideration, especially one made by a jury in a court of law.

words.ex: Please verify your email address.
words.ex_cn: 请核实你的电子邮件地址。
words.en: To verify something means to check or prove that it is true, accurate, or justified.

words.tr: adj. 可核实的；能证实的
words.ex: The result must be verifiable by anyone.
words.ex_cn: 这个结果必须能被任何人验证。
words.en: Capable of being verified or confirmed by evidence or testimony.

chapters.name: 词根 517. verb = word 词语

words.ex: He gave a verbal warning instead of a written one.
words.ex_cn: 他给了一个口头警告，而不是书面的。
words.en: Relating to or in the form of words.

words.ex: He told me a proverb: 'Slow and steady wins the race.'
words.ex_cn: 他告诉我一句谚语：‘慢而稳，胜千里。’
words.en: A proverb is a short, commonly known saying that expresses a truth or piece of advice.

words.tr: adj. 谚语的；众所周知的；已成话柄的
words.ex: It's a proverbial saying that early to bed makes you healthy.
words.ex_cn: 早睡早起是一个谚语，说这样会让你健康。
words.en: Something that is proverbial is well-known by a lot of people, often because it is a typical example of something.

chapters.name: 词根 518. verg = incline 倾向于

words.ex: The car stopped at the verge of the road.
words.ex_cn: 汽车停在了道路的边缘。
words.en: The edge or border of something; to be close to a certain state or condition.

words.ex: The two roads converge at the town center.
words.ex_cn: 这两条路在镇中心交汇。
words.en: If roads or lines converge, they meet or join at a particular place.

chapters.name: 词根 519. vert, vers = turn 转

words.ex: The adverse weather delayed the flight.
words.ex_cn: 不利的天气延误了航班。
words.en: If something is adverse, it is harmful or unfavorable.

words.ex: He turned his head to avert the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他转过头去避免了事故。
words.en: If you avert something unpleasant, you prevent it from happening.

words.ex: There was a controversy about the new school rules.
words.ex_cn: 关于新校规，人们展开了争论。
words.en: A controversy is a disagreement or argument about something that involves many people and generates strong feelings.

words.ex: He controverts the claim with clear evidence.
words.ex_cn: 他用清晰的证据反驳了这一说法。
words.en: To argue about (a subject) in a formal manner; to dispute or contradict.

words.ex: He converts old paper into new notebooks.
words.ex_cn: 他把旧纸张转换成新笔记本。
words.en: To change something into a different form or to change someone's beliefs, especially their religious beliefs.

words.ex: The conversion of water into steam takes heat.
words.ex_cn: 水变成蒸汽需要热量。
words.en: The process of changing or causing something to change from one form to another.

words.ex: The company plans to diversify its products.
words.ex_cn: 公司计划使产品多样化。
words.en: To diversify means to make or become more varied or different. It often refers to the process of a company or individual expanding their range of products or activities to reduce risk or to explore new opportunities.

words.ex: The road was diverted around the park.
words.ex_cn: 这条路被改道绕过公园。
words.en: If you divert someone or something, you cause them to change direction or to go somewhere different.

words.ex: The loud music was a diversion from his worries.
words.ex_cn: 那嘈杂的音乐分散了他对烦恼的注意力。
words.en: A diversion is an action or event that attracts your attention away from what you are doing or should be doing.

words.ex: The speed is inversely proportional to the time.
words.ex_cn: 速度与时间成反比。
words.en: In an inverse manner; in the opposite order, direction, or effect.

words.ex: He tries to invert the numbers to find the answer.
words.ex_cn: 他试图将数字倒过来以找到答案。
words.en: To invert something means to turn it upside down or to reverse its position, order, or relationship.

words.ex: The inversion of the matrix is difficult.
words.ex_cn: 矩阵的逆矩阵很难求。
words.en: An inversion is a change in the position, order, or relationship of things so that they are the opposite of what they were before.

words.tr: adj. 公开的；明显的；公然的
words.ex: His anger was overt and hard to miss.
words.ex_cn: 他的愤怒是明显的，很难忽视。
words.en: An overt action or attitude is done or shown in an open and obvious way.

words.tr:
n. 反面；
v. 使倒转；（使）倒车；撤销；
words.ex: The reverse of the coin has a picture of a tree.
words.ex_cn: 硬币的反面有一棵树的图案。
words.en: If you reverse the order of a set of things, you arrange them in the opposite order, so that the first thing comes last.

words.tr:
adj. 横向的；横放的；横切的
n. 横向物；横断面
words.ex: The transverse line cuts the circle in two parts.
words.ex_cn: 横线将圆分成两部分。
words.en: Situated or extending across something.

words.ex: They traverse the forest to reach the village.
words.ex_cn: 他们横穿森林去到达村庄。
words.en: To traverse something means to move or travel across it, often with some difficulty.

words.tr: adj. 能越过的；可否认的，可反驳的
words.ex: The path is traversable even in rain.
words.ex_cn: 这条小路即使在雨天也能通行。
words.en: Capable of being crossed or passed over.

words.tr: adj. 多方面的；有多种技能的；
words.ex: He is a versatile player who can play many positions.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名多方面的运动员，能打多个位置。
words.en: Able to adapt or be adapted to many different functions or activities.

words.tr: n. 多才多艺；多样性；多功能
words.ex: The tool shows great versatility in different tasks.
words.ex_cn: 这个工具在不同任务中表现出极大的多功能性。
words.en: The ability to adapt or be adapted to many different functions or activities.

words.ex: He writes a verse every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上写一首诗。
words.en: A verse is one of the parts into which a poem, a song, or a chapter of the Bible or the Koran is divided.

words.ex: This is the latest version of the app.
words.ex_cn: 这是这个应用的最新版本。
words.en: A version of something is a particular form of it in which some details are different from earlier or later forms.

words.ex: The tree grows in a vertical line.
words.ex_cn: 这棵树垂直生长。
words.en: Something that is vertical stands or points straight up.

chapters.name: 词根 520. vi = force 力量

words.ex: He violated the school rule by using his phone in class.
words.ex_cn: 他上课使用手机，违反了校规。
words.en: If someone violates an agreement, law, or promise, they break it.

words.tr: n. 违反；妨碍；侵犯；违背；
words.ex: The driver got a ticket for traffic violation.
words.ex_cn: 司机因违反交通规则被开罚单。
words.en: A violation is an action that breaks a law, agreement, principle, etc.

chapters.name: 词根 521. vi, vey = way 道路

words.ex: He conveyed his thanks with a smile.
words.ex_cn: 他微笑着表达了谢意。
words.en: If you convey information or a message, you communicate it to someone, often in a way that is not direct.

words.ex: The car deviated from the road.
words.ex_cn: 汽车偏离了道路。
words.en: To deviate means to do something that is different from the usual or common way of behaving.

words.ex: The deviation from the plan caused delays.
words.ex_cn: 偏离计划导致了延误。
words.en: A deviation is a noticeable difference from what is expected or from a standard.

words.tr: n. （政党内）路线偏差分子; adj. 路线偏差分子的
words.ex: He was labeled a deviationist for questioning the rules.
words.ex_cn: 他因质疑规则而被贴上异端分子的标签。
words.en: A deviationist is someone who deviates from the accepted or official policy or doctrine, especially in politics.

words.ex: The mistake was trivial and didn't affect the result.
words.ex_cn: 这个错误不重要，没有影响结果。
words.en: If you describe something as trivial, you mean that it is not important or significant, or is not worth serious consideration.

words.tr: n. 琐碎；琐事；微不足道
words.ex: He ignored the triviality of the mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他忽略了这个错误的微不足道。
words.en: The quality or state of being trivial or of little importance.

chapters.name: 词根 522. vicin = neighboring 相邻的

words.ex: The park is in the vicinity of my house.
words.ex_cn: 公园在我家附近。
words.en: The area or region near or about a place; the surrounding district.

chapters.name: 词根 523. vict, vinc = conquer 征服

words.ex: His conviction that honesty is important never changed.
words.ex_cn: 他坚信诚实很重要，从未改变。
words.en: A conviction is a strong belief or opinion, or the state of being found guilty of a crime in a court of law.

words.ex: He tried to convince her to stay.
words.ex_cn: 他试图说服她留下。
words.en: If someone or something convinces you of something, they make you believe that it is true or that it exists.

chapters.name: 词根 524. vid = separate 分开

words.tr: n. 被除数；股份红利；股息
words.ex: In 12 ÷ 3 = 4, the dividend is 12.
words.en: A dividend is a sum of money paid regularly (typically annually) by a company to its shareholders out of its profits (or reserves).

words.tr:
n. 个人；
adj. 个别的；单独的；
words.ex: Each individual has the right to speak freely.
words.ex_cn: 每个人都有权自由发言。
words.en: An individual is a person considered separately from their society or community. As an adjective, it describes something that is single, separate, or unique to a person or thing.

words.ex: He will subdivide the land into two parts.
words.ex_cn: 他将把土地分成两部分。
words.en: If something is subdivided, it is divided into several smaller areas, parts, or sections.

words.ex: The company made a subdivision of its market by age.
words.ex_cn: 公司按年龄对市场进行了细分。
words.en: A subdivision is a part or section of something which is itself divided into parts.

chapters.name: 词根 525. vig, vit, viv = life 生命

words.ex: The medicine helped revive the sick man.
words.ex_cn: 这剂药帮助这位病人恢复了生机。
words.en: To revive something means to bring it back to life, consciousness, or use, or to make it active or successful again.

words.ex: The revival of traditional music brought joy to many people.
words.ex_cn: 传统音乐的复兴给许多人带来了快乐。
words.en: The process of something becoming popular or active again after a period of inactivity or decline.

words.ex: The survival of the animals depends on the weather.
words.ex_cn: 这些动物的生存取决于天气。
words.en: The state or fact of continuing to live or exist, typically in spite of an accident, ordeal, or difficult circumstances.

words.tr: adj. 精力充沛的；茂盛的；
words.ex: He is a vigorous man who runs every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个精力充沛的人，每天早上都跑步。
words.en: A vigorous person does things with great energy and enthusiasm. A vigorous campaign or activity is done with great energy and enthusiasm.

words.ex: The child shows great vitality while playing.
words.ex_cn: 孩子玩耍时充满活力。
words.en: Vitality refers to the state of being strong and active; energy.

words.tr: v. 给予 ... 生命力； 激发
words.ex: The new paint will vitalize the old house.
words.ex_cn: 新油漆会让这栋老房子焕然一新。
words.en: To give life or energy to something, making it more active or successful.

chapters.name: 词根 526. vis = see 看

words.ex: I envisage a world without war.
words.ex_cn: 我设想一个没有战争的世界。
words.en: If you envisage something, you imagine that it is true, real, or likely to happen.

words.ex: The ship carries a provision of food for the journey.
words.ex_cn: 这艘船为旅程准备了食物供应。
words.en: A provision is a condition or requirement in a legal document. It can also refer to the act of supplying or providing something that is needed.

words.ex: The teacher supervises the students during the experiment.
words.ex_cn: 老师在实验期间指导学生。
words.en: If you supervise an activity or a person, you make sure that the activity is done correctly or that the person is doing a task or behaving correctly.

words.ex: The teacher gave supervision to the students during the exam.
words.ex_cn: 老师在考试期间监督学生。
words.en: The act of overseeing or directing a project, activity, or person.

words.ex: He needs a visa to travel to Japan.
words.ex_cn: 他需要一张签证去日本旅行。
words.en: A visa is an official document, or a stamp put in your passport, which allows you to enter or leave a particular country.

words.tr: v. 使可见；使形象化；设想；
words.ex: He uses maps to visualize the data.
words.ex_cn: 他使用地图来使数据可见。
words.en: If you visualize something, you imagine what it is like by forming a mental picture of it.

words.tr: n. 可视化；视觉化；形象化
words.ex: He uses visualization to understand the data.
words.ex_cn: 他使用可视化来理解数据。
words.en: Visualization is the process of making something able to be seen or easily imagined.

chapters.name: 词根 527. voc, vok = call, voice 叫喊，声音

words.tr:
n. 提倡者；
v. 提倡；
words.ex: He is an advocate for clean water.
words.ex_cn: 他是清洁用水的提倡者。
words.en: If you advocate a particular action or plan, you recommend it publicly.

words.ex: He supports advocacy for clean water.
words.ex_cn: 他支持清洁用水的倡导。
words.en: The act of pleading or arguing in favor of something, such as a cause, idea, or policy; active support.

words.ex: The song evokes happy memories of childhood.
words.ex_cn: 这首歌唤起了对童年的美好回忆。
words.en: To evoke a particular memory, idea, emotion, or response means to cause it to occur.

words.ex: His rude words provoked her anger.
words.ex_cn: 他粗鲁的话激怒了她。
words.en: If you provoke someone, you deliberately annoy them and try to make them behave aggressively.

words.ex: His provocative words made everyone angry.
words.ex_cn: 他挑衅的话让所有人都生气了。
words.en: If you describe something as provocative, you mean that it is intended to make people react angrily or argue against it.

words.ex: His rude comment was a provocation to start a fight.
words.ex_cn: 他粗鲁的评论是一种挑衅，想引发争斗。
words.en: If you describe someone's action as a provocation, you mean that it is likely to cause a reaction or argument, especially a violent or angry one.

words.ex: The teacher will revoke his privilege to use the computer.
words.ex_cn: 老师将撤销他使用电脑的权限。
words.en: If someone in authority revokes something such as a law, license, or agreement, they cancel it.

words.tr: adj. 发声的；嗓音的；直言不讳的；
words.ex: He made a vocal sound to get attention.
words.ex_cn: 他发出声音来引起注意。
words.en: If you are vocal about something, you express your opinions or feelings about it in a strong and public way.

words.ex: He is learning vocational skills to become a mechanic.
words.ex_cn: 他正在学习职业技能以成为一名机械师。
words.en: Relating to the skills you need to do a particular job.

chapters.name: 词根 528. volunt = will 意愿

words.tr:
n. 志愿者；
v. 自愿做；
words.ex: He is a volunteer at the local hospital.
words.ex_cn: 他是当地医院的一名志愿者。
words.en: A volunteer is someone who does work without being paid for it, especially work that involves helping people.

words.ex: He did voluntary work at the hospital.
words.ex_cn: 他在医院做志愿工作。
words.en: If something is voluntary, you do it because you choose to, and not because you have to.

chapters.name: 词根 529. volu, volv = roll 滚

words.ex: The evolution of birds from dinosaurs took millions of years.
words.ex_cn: 鸟类从恐龙进化而来花了数百万年。
words.en: The gradual development of something, especially from a simple to a more complex form.

words.ex: The Earth revolves around the Sun.
words.ex_cn: 地球围绕太阳转。
words.en: If something revolves or if you revolve something, it moves or turns around a central point or line.

chapters.name: 词根 530. vor = eat 吃

words.tr: v. 吞食；吞噬；狼吞虎咽地吃；如饥似渴地看
words.ex: The dog devoured the meat quickly.
words.ex_cn: 狗很快地把肉吃光了。
words.en: To eat something quickly and eagerly, especially because you are very hungry; to destroy something quickly and completely.

chapters.name: 词根 531. vot = vow 发誓

words.ex: His devotion to his family is obvious.
words.ex_cn: 他对家庭的献身显而易见。
words.en: Devotion is great love, affection, or admiration for someone or something.

chapters.name: 联想

words.tr:
n. 青少年；
adj. 青少年的；
words.ex: The adolescent walked to school with his friends.
words.ex_cn: 这个青少年和朋友们一起走路去上学。
words.en: An adolescent is a young person who is developing into an adult.

words.ex: He was shy during his adolescence.
words.ex_cn: 他在青春期时很害羞。
words.en: Adolescence is the period in a person's life when they develop from a child into an adult.

words.ex: The room has air-conditioning to keep it cool.
words.ex_cn: 这个房间有空调来保持凉爽。
words.en: a system that keeps the air in a building cool and dry

words.ex: The books are on the shelf beside the aisle.
words.ex_cn: 书在过道旁边的架子上。
words.en: An aisle is a long narrow gap that people can walk along between rows of seats in a public building such as a church or between rows of shelves in a supermarket.

words.ex: My parents give me a weekly allowance.
words.ex_cn: 我父母每周给我零用钱。
words.en: An allowance is money that is given regularly, usually to a child, by their parents, or by the government to someone who is unemployed or ill.

words.tr:
n. 合金
v. 把…铸成合金
words.ex: He made a strong alloy from copper and zinc.
words.ex_cn: 他用铜和锌制造了一种坚固的合金。
words.en: An alloy is a metal made by combining two or more metallic elements, especially to give greater strength or resistance to corrosion.

words.ex: He gave her a gift to appease her anger.
words.ex_cn: 他送她一份礼物来平息她的怒气。
words.en: If you try to appease someone, you try to stop them from being angry by giving them what they want.

words.ex: The government tried appeasement to calm the protests.
words.ex_cn: 政府试图通过平息来安抚抗议活动。
words.en: The action or process of appeasing.

words.ex: The kitchen has a new washing appliance.
words.ex_cn: 厨房里有一台新的洗衣机。
words.en: An appliance is a device or machine that is used to perform a particular task, especially in the home.

words.ex: His answer was apt for the question.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答对这个问题很恰当。
words.en: If someone is apt to do something, they often do it and so it is likely that they will do it again.

words.ex: He aptly answered the question.
words.ex_cn: 他恰当地回答了问题。
words.en: In a manner that is appropriate or suitable in the circumstances.

words.ex: The ant moved its antenna to feel the ground.
words.ex_cn: 蚂蚁用它的触角感知地面。
words.en: An antenna is a device that sends and receives radio or television signals. In biology, it refers to the long, thin sensory appendages on the heads of insects and crustaceans.

words.ex: The insect moves its antennal segments to feel the air.
words.ex_cn: 昆虫移动它的触角节来感知空气。
words.en: Relating to or resembling an antenna.

words.ex: The boxing match took place in an arena.
words.ex_cn: 拳击比赛在竞技场举行。
words.en: An arena is a place or scene of activity, debate, or conflict, especially one where a competition or performance is held.

words.ex: There was an array of people at the concert.
words.ex_cn: 音乐会上人山人海。
words.en: An array of different things or people is a large number or wide range of them.

words.ex: The artery carries blood from the heart.
words.ex_cn: 动脉将血液从心脏输送到身体。
words.en: An artery is a tube that carries blood from the heart to the rest of the body.

words.ex: He can articulate his ideas clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他能清楚地表达自己的想法。
words.en: If you describe someone as articulate, you mean that they are able to express their thoughts and ideas easily and clearly.

words.ex: The king's assassination shocked the whole country.
words.ex_cn: 国王的暗杀震惊了整个国家。
words.en: The act of killing someone important or famous, often for political reasons.

words.ex: The teacher gave an assessment of the students' work.
words.ex_cn: 老师对学生的作品进行了评估。
words.en: An assessment is a judgment about something, especially about how good or bad it is, or an amount that is calculated for something, especially for tax purposes.

words.ex: He looked up the country in an atlas.
words.ex_cn: 他在地图册里查找那个国家。
words.en: An atlas is a book of maps or charts.

words.tr: adj. 真正的；真实的；真迹的；可靠的；
words.ex: This is an authentic painting by Picasso.
words.ex_cn: 这是一幅毕加索的真迹。
words.en: If something is authentic, it is real, true, or what people say it is.

words.ex: He felt awkward when he forgot his friend's name.
words.ex_cn: 当他忘记朋友的名字时，他感到很尴尬。
words.en: If you describe a situation as awkward, you mean that it is embarrassing or difficult to deal with.

words.ex: The Earth rotates around its axis.
words.ex_cn: 地球围绕其轴旋转。
words.en: An axis is an imaginary line through the middle of something, especially one that it turns around.

words.ex: He wears a badge on his shirt.
words.ex_cn: 他衬衫上戴着一枚徽章。
words.en: A badge is a small piece of metal, plastic, or cloth which you wear in order to show people that you have a particular rank, job, or belong to a particular group.

words.tr:
v. 使困惑；难倒；阻碍
n. 挡板；遮护物；阻碍体
words.ex: The magic trick baffled the children.
words.ex_cn: 这个魔术让孩子们感到困惑。
words.en: If something baffles you, you cannot understand it or explain it.

words.tr: adj. 秃头的；不加修饰的；赤裸裸的
words.ex: The old man is bald.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人是秃头的。
words.en: Someone who is bald has little or no hair on the top of their head.

words.ex: She practices ballet every afternoon.
words.ex_cn: 她每天下午练习芭蕾舞。
words.en: Ballet is a type of performance dance that originated during the Italian Renaissance in the 15th century and later developed into a concert dance form in France and Russia. It has since become a widespread, highly technical form of dance with its own vocabulary based on French terminology. It has been globally influential and has defined the foundational techniques used in many other dance genres.

words.ex: They had a big banquet after the wedding.
words.ex_cn: 婚礼后他们举办了一场盛大的宴会。
words.en: A banquet is a large formal meal for many people, often followed by speeches in honor of someone.

words.ex: The barren land cannot grow any crops.
words.ex_cn: 这片贫瘠的土地无法种植任何庄稼。
words.en: If you describe something as barren, you mean that it is not able to produce anything, especially plants or crops.

words.ex: The bakery made a new batch of bread this morning.
words.ex_cn: 这家面包店今天早上做了一批新面包。
words.en: A batch is a quantity or consignment of goods produced at one time.

words.ex: He rubbed his belly after eating too much.
words.ex_cn: 他吃完太多后揉了揉腹部。
words.en: The belly is the front part of a person's or animal's body between the chest and the legs.

words.tr: v. 背叛；出卖；泄露；暴露
words.ex: He betrays his friend by telling the secret.
words.ex_cn: 他通过泄露秘密背叛了朋友。
words.en: If you betray someone who loves or trusts you, your actions hurt and disappoint them.

words.ex: He was the betrayer of his best friend.
words.ex_cn: 他是背叛最好朋友的人。
words.en: A betrayer is someone who betrays a person, group, or principle, often by revealing secrets or acting against them.

words.ex: Beware of the dog.
words.ex_cn: 当心那只狗。
words.en: to be cautious and alert to the dangers of.

words.tr: v. 使迷惑；使...不知所措
words.ex: The strange signs bewilder the children.
words.ex_cn: 这些奇怪的符号让孩子们感到迷惑。
words.en: If something bewilders you, it is so confusing or difficult that you cannot understand it.

words.tr:
adj. 令人困惑的；使人糊涂的
v. 使迷惑；使昏乱；“bewilder”的现在分词
words.ex: The maze was bewildering.
words.ex_cn: 这个迷宫令人困惑。
words.en: If something is bewildering, it is very confusing and difficult to understand or to make a decision about.

words.tr: adj. 离奇的；奇特的；奇怪的；
words.ex: The clown wore a bizarre hat with three eyes.
words.ex_cn: 小丑戴着一顶有三只眼睛的离奇帽子。
words.en: Something that is bizarre is very odd and strange.

words.ex: The blacksmith makes horseshoes with a hammer.
words.ex_cn: 铁匠用锤子打马蹄铁。
words.en: A blacksmith is a person who makes and repairs things in iron by hand.

words.tr:
n. 烈火；火焰；闪耀
v. 闪耀；熊熊燃烧；发亮光
words.ex: The fire began to blaze in the woods.
words.ex_cn: 火在森林里开始猛烈燃烧。
words.en: A blaze is a very large or fiercely burning fire that is difficult to control.

words.ex: He nodded in a blink.
words.ex_cn: 他一眨眼就点了点头。
words.en: To shut and open the eyes quickly, typically involuntarily.

words.tr:
n. （果树的）花朵；
v. 开花；
words.ex: The apple tree is full of blossom in spring.
words.ex_cn: 春天时，苹果树上开满了花。
words.en: When a tree or plant blossoms, it produces flowers before producing fruit that can be eaten.

words.tr:
n. 愚蠢的错误；失误
v. 犯愚蠢的错误；失误；跌跌撞撞地走
words.ex: He made a big blunder in the math test.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学考试中犯了一个大错误。
words.en: A blunder is a stupid or careless mistake.

words.tr: n. 轻率粗心的人；犯愚蠢错误的人
words.ex: He is a blunderer who makes many mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个总犯很多错误的人。
words.en: A blunderer is someone who makes serious mistakes, especially because of carelessness or lack of skill.

words.tr:
adj. 不锋利的；耿直的
v. 使变钝
words.ex: The knife is blunt and cannot cut paper.
words.ex_cn: 这把刀不锋利，切不动纸。
words.en: If you are blunt, you say exactly what you think without trying to be polite.

words.ex: His bluntness made her feel uncomfortable.
words.ex_cn: 他的直率让她感到不舒服。
words.en: The quality of being blunt, either in the sense of not being sharp or in the sense of being straightforward and direct in speech.

words.tr:
v. 使模糊；使看不清；弄污
n. 模糊
words.ex: The rain made the lights blur.
words.ex_cn: 雨使灯光变得模糊。
words.en: If something blurs your vision, it makes you unable to see things clearly.

words.ex: The photo is blurry because the camera shook.
words.ex_cn: 这张照片很模糊，因为相机晃动了。
words.en: If something is blurry, it is unclear or not sharply defined, often because it is moving too fast or because of a lack of focus.

words.tr:
n. 脸红；羞愧
v. 泛红；羞愧
words.ex: He felt shy and got a blush when she praised him.
words.ex_cn: 当他被她夸奖时，他感到害羞，脸红了。
words.en: If you blush, your face turns red because you are embarrassed or ashamed.

words.ex: He read the booklet about the new rules.
words.ex_cn: 他读了那本关于新规则的小册子。
words.en: A booklet is a small, thin book that has a paper cover and that gives you information about something.

words.ex: He bought a hot dog from a food booth.
words.ex_cn: 他从一个小吃亭买了个热狗。
words.en: A booth is a small area separated from a larger public area by screens or thin walls where, for example, people can make a phone call or vote in private.

words.ex: The doctor checked his bowel for signs of infection.
words.ex_cn: 医生检查了他的肠是否有感染迹象。
words.en: The lower part of the alimentary canal from the end of the stomach to the anus.

words.tr:
n. 抵制；拒绝参加；
v. 抵制；拒绝参加；
words.ex: The students organized a boycott of the unfair school rule.
words.ex_cn: 学生们组织了对这项不公平校规的抵制。
words.en: If a country, group, or person boycotts a country, organization, or activity, they refuse to be involved with it in any way because they disapprove of it.

words.ex: He moved up to a higher bracket after his promotion.
words.ex_cn: 他升职后进入了更高的等级。
words.en: A bracket is a piece of metal, wood, or plastic that is fastened to a wall in order to support something such as a shelf. In writing, brackets are symbols that are used to separate words or numbers.

words.tr:
n. 违背；
v. 攻破；
words.ex: The company committed a breach of contract.
words.ex_cn: 该公司违反了合同。
words.en: A breach of a law, rule, or agreement is an act of breaking it.

words.ex: The scientist made a breakthrough in cancer research.
words.ex_cn: 这位科学家在癌症研究中取得了突破。
words.en: A breakthrough is a significant development or achievement that helps to solve a problem or improve a situation.

words.tr:
v. 交配繁殖；饲养；
n. 品种；
words.ex: The farmers breed cows to get more milk.
words.ex_cn: 农民让奶牛交配繁殖以获得更多牛奶。
words.en: If you breed animals or plants, you keep them for the purpose of producing more animals or plants with particular qualities, in a controlled way.

words.tr: n. 繁殖者；饲养员；起因
words.ex: The breeder takes care of dogs every day.
words.ex_cn: 繁育者每天照顾狗。
words.en: A breeder is a person who breeds animals or plants professionally.

words.tr:
v. 酿造；沏；酝酿
n. 酿造的饮料；啤酒
words.ex: He brews coffee every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上冲咖啡。
words.en: If you brew tea or coffee, you make it by pouring hot water over tea leaves or ground coffee. If you brew beer, you make it by soaking grain in water and then fermenting it.

words.ex: He tried to bribe the officer with money.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用钱贿赂官员。
words.en: A bribe is a sum of money or something valuable that one person offers or gives to another in order to persuade them to do something, usually something dishonest.

words.ex: He went to jail for bribery.
words.ex_cn: 他因贿赂而入狱。
words.en: Bribery is the act of offering, giving, receiving, or soliciting something of value for the purpose of influencing the action of an official in the discharge of his or her public or legal duties.

words.ex: The country is on the brink of war.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家正处于战争的边缘。
words.en: If you are on the brink of something, you are about to do it or experience it.

words.ex: He took a brisk walk in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 他早上轻快地散步。
words.en: If someone or something is brisk, they are quick and lively in their actions or movements.

words.ex: He picked up a brochure about the city.
words.ex_cn: 他拿了一本关于这座城市的宣传小册子。
words.en: A brochure is a type of small magazine or booklet containing pictures and information about something or advertising something.

words.ex: The statue is made of bronze.
words.ex_cn: 这座雕像由青铜制成。
words.en: Bronze is a yellowish-brown metal which is a mixture of copper and tin.

words.tr: v. 沉思；闷闷不乐地想；n. 一窝幼崽；沉思的状态
words.ex: He sits by the window and broods over his failures.
words.ex_cn: 他坐在窗边，为自己的失败而忧思。
words.en: If someone broods over something, they think about it a lot, seriously and often unhappily. A brood is a group of young birds all born at the same time to the same mother.

words.tr: adj. 孵卵的；多产的；多思考的
words.ex: The hen is broody and won't leave her eggs.
words.ex_cn: 这只母鸡想孵蛋，不愿离开它的蛋。
words.en: If you describe someone as broody, you mean that they are thinking deeply and seriously about something, often in a way that seems moody or unhappy.

words.tr: v. 擦伤；挫伤；出现伤痕；
words.ex: He bruised his knee when he fell off the bike.
words.ex_cn: 他从自行车上摔下来时擦伤了膝盖。
words.en: A bruise is a mark that appears on your skin after you have been injured, but the skin is not broken.

words.ex: The storm caused a brutal flood that destroyed many homes.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴引发了残酷的洪水，摧毁了许多房屋。
words.en: A brutal act or person is cruel and violent.

words.ex: The movie shows the brutality of war.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影展示了战争的残忍。
words.en: Brutality is cruel and violent behavior, or a cruel and violent act.

words.tr:
n. 雄鹿；公羊；雄兔；美元
v. （马等）猛然弓背跃起；抵制
words.ex: The buck ran through the forest.
words.ex_cn: 雄鹿在森林中奔跑。
words.en: A buck is a male deer, antelope, rabbit, or hare. It can also refer to a dollar in American slang. As a verb, it means to jump or to resist something.

words.ex: The trees bud in spring.
words.ex_cn: 树木在春天发芽。
words.en: A bud is a small pointed lump that appears on a tree or plant and develops into a leaf or flower.

words.tr:
n. 预算；预算金额；
adj. 廉价的；花钱少的；
v. 为 ... 做预算；
words.ex: We made a budget for our vacation.
words.ex_cn: 我们为旅行制定了一个预算。
words.en: A budget is a plan that shows how much money a person or organization will earn and how much they will need or be able to spend.

words.ex: The school has a tight budgetary plan.
words.ex_cn: 学校有一个紧张的预算计划。
words.en: Relating to or involving a budget, especially of a government or organization.

words.tr: n. 公告；布告；公报；新闻简报；
words.ex: The school posted a bulletin about the holiday schedule.
words.ex_cn: 学校张贴了一份关于假期安排的公告。
words.en: A bulletin is a short news report on the radio or television. A bulletin is also a short printed newspaper or leaflet that gives information about a particular group or organization.

words.ex: He bullies his little brother every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天都欺负他的弟弟。
words.en: To bully someone means to use your strength or power to hurt or frighten them, often forcing them to do something they do not want to do.

words.tr:
v. 撞；碰上；颠簸行进；
n. 碰撞；猛击；肿块；凸块；
words.ex: He bumped the table and spilled his drink.
words.ex_cn: 他撞到了桌子，打翻了饮料。
words.en: If you bump into something or someone, you accidentally hit them while you are moving.

words.ex: The burial took place at sunrise.
words.ex_cn: 埋葬在日出时进行。
words.en: The act or ceremony of putting a dead body into a grave.

words.tr:
n. 半身像；胸部；搜捕
v. 打碎；搜捕
adj. 破产的；打碎的
words.ex: The museum has a marble bust of the ancient king.
words.ex_cn: 博物馆里有一座古代国王的大理石半身像。
words.en: A bust is a sculpture of a person's head, shoulders, and chest. As a verb, to bust means to break something, to arrest someone, or to go bankrupt.

words.ex: The bees made a loud buzz near the flowers.
words.ex_cn: 蜜蜂在花附近发出嗡嗡声。
words.en: To make a low, continuous, humming or sibilant sound, like that made by bees or flies.

words.tr:
